title: Paper trading & demo/live parity
body:
## Context
R3 "Trading on demo" executes **everything** against Bybit demo; there is no code path that can reach live until R4 flips the gate (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` section 7). E38 is the epic that owns that statement. It is simultaneously:

1. **The environment boundary.** SCR-075 is described in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` as "the single most safety-critical visual element in the app", and `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` SR-040a requires the environment capability matrix to be "enforced in code, not documentation". Threats **W9** (code assuming WS order entry exists on demo, leaving orders unplaced or duplicated) and **W10** (demo and live endpoints mixed within one session) are named in the security program with this epic's work as their control.
2. **The honest simulator.** `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 12 specifies the local paper matcher (module **M16**) field by field - queue position, latency, fees, funding, margin - because a simulator that ignores those lies, and a lying simulator is worse than none: it manufactures confidence (risk **R12**).
3. **The parity evidence base.** US-PAPER-008's report is what makes R4 "a gating exercise rather than a re-architecture" (roadmap section 7.1 goal 5). The roadmap dependency graph records `E38 --> E44`: whatever this epic leaves ambiguous becomes a live-money problem in R4.

The epic sits at S18-S19, the last two sprints of R3, and depends on `E29` (OMS and order state machine) and `E26` (replay engine) per the roadmap's dependency graph.

## Scope / Deliverables
**User stories covered (all Must/Should in the PAPER domain, `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` section 21):**
- **US-PAPER-001** Bybit demo integration (Must) - E38-S01
- **US-PAPER-002** Explicit Demo/Live switching (Must) - E38-S02 (backend), E38-S04 (UI)
- **US-PAPER-003** Demo/Live isolation gating (Must) - E38-T02 (server enforcement), E38-S04 (client guard)
- **US-PAPER-004** Local simulated fill engine (Should) - E38-S03, E38-S05
- **US-PAPER-005** Paper P&L identical to live (Must) - E38-S03 (same accounting path), E38-S05 (separate reporting and labelling)
- **US-PAPER-006** Reset paper balance (Should) - E38-S06
- **US-PAPER-007** Demo eligibility per manager (Should) - E38-S07
- **US-PAPER-008** Environment parity report (Should) - E38-K01, E38-S08, E38-T03

**Screens:** SCR-074 Environment switcher, SCR-075 Demo/Live banner and per-panel badges, SCR-079 Account detail drawer (reset section), SCR-099 Replay paper-trading results, SCR-122 Admin user detail (eligibility section), SCR-137 Admin security centre (parity + fidelity sections).

**Components:** CMP-074 EnvBanner, CMP-075 EnvBadgeLocal, CMP-139 EnvironmentAwareOrderGuard, plus composition of CMP-027, CMP-028, CMP-036, CMP-043, CMP-044, CMP-049, CMP-050, CMP-087, CMP-093, CMP-099, CMP-104, CMP-106, CMP-116, CMP-128, CMP-129, CMP-167, CMP-168, CMP-175, CMP-178; contributes a new simulated badge to the design system.

**Backend module:** **M16 Paper Matcher** (`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` section 3.7, C11) - `FillModel`, `QueueEstimator`, `FeeModel`, `PaperLedger` - plus the environment capability matrix and the isolation middleware.

**API:** `POST /session/environment` (implemented), `PUT /users/{userId}/account-access` (extended with eligibility), and new: `POST /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/paper-reset`, `GET /admin/parity` plus its verification endpoint, `GET /admin/paper-fidelity`. Environment enforcement is applied to every account-mutating trading route.

**WS:** `system` topic (environment switch phases and the resulting environment), `is_paper` on every private frame (`docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` section 13.1).

**DB:** `exchange_accounts.env`, `is_paper` columns across orders/positions/executions/trade groups, `user_account_access` extended with live eligibility and its acknowledgement, paper ledger and parity-observation storage.

## Out of scope
- **Live order entry.** The `live_trading` flag stays off through R3; turning it on is E44 after the E43 pen-test.
- **Android and any separate admin application** - owner decisions, permanently out of scope.
- Non-USDT-perp products (spot, options, inverse).
- Resetting a Bybit demo account's balance at the exchange - only the local paper ledger is reset.
- Auto-tuning the fill model from divergence results; tuning stays a human decision.
- Journal analytics computation (E41), replay transport (E26), fan-out (E34), the OMS itself (E29) - E38 consumes them.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Demo and live can never mix
  Given a session in one environment
  When any account-mutating trading route is called against an account in the other environment, including by a crafted request bypassing the UI
  Then it is refused with 403, no state changes, and a high-severity audit row is written - proven across every trading route by an automated route-coverage test

Scenario: Switching to live is deliberate, gated and complete
  Given a session in demo
  When the user switches to live
  Then it requires a typed confirmation phrase, step-up authentication and the live_trading flag; no hotkey can trigger it; one-click trading is disarmed; every private subscription is torn down and rebuilt; and a half-switched state is never reachable, including across a backend restart mid-transition

Scenario: The environment is stated on every trading-capable surface
  Given any trading panel, including floated and maximised Electron windows
  When it is rendered
  Then it states DEMO or LIVE in text plus icon plus pattern, remains unambiguous in greyscale and in three colour-vision simulations, and includes the environment in its accessible name

Scenario: The simulator is honest and can never reach the exchange
  Given the paper matcher
  When orders are simulated
  Then fills respect queue position, latency, book depth, real fee rates and funding; the applied FillModelConfig is disclosed with every result set; a structural test proves the paper package imports no network client; and a nightly divergence job compares simulated against real demo fills, opening a defect above one tick p95 slippage or ten percentage points fill-rate divergence

Scenario: Paper results never contaminate live statistics
  Given a journal containing both simulated and real trades
  When analytics are computed
  Then simulated rows are excluded by default, every view labels them, and promotion of a simulated session to the journal is flagged and audited

Scenario: The parity report is generated and current
  Given the maintained parity data file plus runtime observations
  When the report is viewed
  Then every known difference is listed with its source and last-verified date, demo-only failures appear as candidate items, and items unverified for 90 days are flagged

Scenario: Eligibility is a server-side attribute with safe revocation
  Given a manager without live eligibility
  Then no live action succeeds by any path; and when live access is revoked while live positions are open, those positions remain manageable in reduce-only mode while new entries are refused
```

## Technical notes / design
- **One code path, two environments.** The only environment-aware code is the adapter's immutable capability record and key selection; an architecture test asserts the string `demo` does not appear in `cv/oms/`. This is what makes R4 a gate flip rather than a rewrite.
- **One choke point.** Environment enforcement lives in a single FastAPI dependency (E38-T02) that returns an `EnvironmentContext` handlers must accept, so omission is a type error. A route-coverage test over the OpenAPI document fails CI when a new trading route lacks it.
- **`is_paper` is orthogonal to `environment`.** A paper fill still belongs to a real environment (demo, or live when replaying live-recorded data). `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` section 13.1 is explicit that collapsing them would lose information; the UI must therefore show two distinct badges.
- **The matcher rides the shared bus.** Replay re-emits recorded events with the same types onto the same bus (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 13), so the matcher works identically over live and recorded data, and its determinism supports R3 exit criterion 6.
- **Structural versus enforced controls.** E38-X01 classifies each control; structural controls (separate client instances, no transport import in `cv/paper/`) get import-time or compile-time tests, enforced controls get runtime tests. The distinction drives the regression pack.

## Test plan
- **Unit** - queue estimator table-driven suite (the highest-value set in the epic), book walk VWAP, latency races, fee and funding maths, liquidation tiers, environment refusal matrix, eligibility derivation, staleness boundaries. Coverage: >=90% on `cv/paper/` and the safety-critical middleware, >=85% backend elsewhere, >=80% frontend.
- **Contract** - `enum_parity_environment`, the new endpoints, error-registry entries, WS frame shapes, and the route-coverage gate.
- **Integration** - recorded demo fixtures for submit/partial-fill/amend/cancel/reject/reconnect; replay-driven matcher sessions with restart recovery; reset atomicity; revocation with open positions.
- **E2E** - nine Playwright suites across web and Electron (E38-Q02), including the crafted cross-environment request and the floating-window badge.
- **Perf** - budget #4 (submit-to-ack p95 <300 ms on demo, hard R3 gate), matcher throughput at >=20x real time, switch transition p95 <=2 s, memory budget #8 (E38-Q03).
- **Chaos** - restart mid-switch at each phase, WS disconnect mid-order, restart with open simulated state, Postgres failure mid-reset, audit-writer failure must fail closed, clock skew, WS flapping during a switch (E38-Q04).
- **Security** - STRIDE (E38-X01), abuse cases plus durable Semgrep/ZAP rules (E38-X02), review and sign-off (E38-X03).
- **A11y** - axe-core in CI per state plus NVDA manual passes (E38-Q05).

## Security notes
- STRIDE model at `docs/security/threat-models/E38-paper-trading.md` (E38-X01). Highest-rated threats: a simulated order reaching the exchange (Critical), a demo session reaching live (Critical), a manager self-granting live eligibility (High), an unaudited environment switch or reset (High), a not-permitted message disclosing other users' grants (Medium).
- Implements **SR-040a** (environment capability matrix in code), supports **SR-119** (single backend chokepoint for exchange traffic) and **SR-043** (armed state for live). Demo keys are handled identically to live keys (SR-003, SR-004); CI never holds demo credentials (SR-140).
- Every ticket touching RBAC, order placement or account-scoped state carries the `security` label per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 8, and cannot reach Done without a Security engineer review.
- Data classification: financial transaction and simulation data; API credentials by reference only; no secret is rendered on any E38 surface.

## Accessibility notes
- WCAG 2.2 AA across all six surfaces, with no "internal tool" exception for the admin screens.
- The environment distinction must be text plus icon plus pattern, unambiguous in greyscale and in deuteranopia, protanopia and tritanopia simulations - verified in design (E38-D05) and on the built app (E38-Q05).
- The band is `role="status"` and polite; the post-switch confirmation is `role="alert"` announced once; per-panel badges are `role="img"` with static labels to prevent an announcement storm.
- Every SCR-099 chart has a keyboard-reachable table alternative; the destructive reset dialog announces the counts it will discard and does not default focus to the destructive button.
- An imperceptible environment indicator is treated as a security defect, not only an accessibility one.

## Performance notes
- Budget **#4** order submit to ack p95 <300 ms on demo is a **hard R3 exit gate**; E38-S01 owns it and E38-Q03 measures it with backend-internal and exchange-RTT components separated.
- Budget **#8** <=300 MB resident per actively-recorded symbol during matcher replay; budget **#15** replay at up to 100x without the matcher becoming the bottleneck.
- The environment switch blocks order entry for its whole duration - p95 <=2 s per SCR-074, measured per phase.
- The environment band must not remount on route change and an environment change must not re-render trading panel bodies; re-badging must not breach frame budget **#1**.

## Observability
- Metrics: `cv_capability_refusals_total`, `cv_environment_rejections_total`, `cv_environment_switch_duration_seconds`, `cv_environment_switch_failures_total`, `cv_orders_submitted_total{environment}`, `cv_order_ack_latency_seconds{environment}`, `cv_paper_fills_total`, `cv_paper_rejections_total`, `cv_paper_resets_total`, `cv_paper_divergence_*`, `cv_parity_items{status}`, `cv_live_eligible_users`.
- Audit events: `session.environment_switched`, `session.environment_switch_refused`, `trading.environment_mismatch_rejected`, `paper.balance_reset`, `paper.balance_reset_refused`, `user.live_access_granted|revoked|acknowledged`, `parity.item_verified`, `journal.simulated_import`.
- Alerts: divergence threshold breach, missed divergence run, demo private WS disconnected with open orders, audit-writer failure, clock skew beyond 1000 ms.

## Sizing
- The roadmap registers E38 at **26 points** (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` line 138 and section 7.2). Engineering children (Story/Task/Spike: K01 2, S01 2, S02 2, S03 5, S04 3, S05 1, S06 1, S07 2, S08 2, T01 2, T02 3, T03 2, T04 1) now total **28 points** - +7.7% against the registered sizing and inside the +/-15% tolerance band of `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md`.
- The reduction from 30 comes from re-sizing E38-S05 and E38-S06 from 2 to 1 each; both are thin consumers of work owned elsewhere (E38-S03's matcher payload, E38-D04's badge component, E41's charts) and their bodies record the rationale. No scope was dropped.
- Design, QA and security children (D01-D07, Q01-Q06, X01-X03) carry a further 37 points of discipline effort tracked outside the engineering sizing; the epic `estimate` field carries the full child rollup of **65**.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every child ticket Done (100% rollup) or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] Epic-level acceptance criteria verified end to end on staging (demo), not merely per child.
- [ ] Coverage floors held: >=90% on `cv/paper/` and the safety-critical middleware, >=85% backend, >=80% frontend; zero open P0/P1 against E38 scope.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core CI green on all six surfaces and states, manual NVDA passes recorded, colour-vision verification on the built app (E38-Q05).
- [ ] perf: budgets #1, #4, #8, #15 and the switch transition measured and recorded against `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` (E38-Q03).
- [ ] security: STRIDE finalised, all Critical/High findings closed or Owner-accepted with expiry, Security engineer sign-off, durable Semgrep/ZAP rules running as required checks (E38-X01..X03).
- [ ] QA: epic-level regression pack and both exploratory charters executed with recorded sign-off (E38-Q06).
- [ ] design: all design tickets Done >=2 sprints ahead of their consuming stories; design QA complete with discrepancies closed (E38-D07).
- [ ] Docs reconciled with shipped behaviour and ADR-0016 amended (E38-T04); `make contracts` green.
- [ ] R4 handover statement written: what E38 guarantees about environment separation, what it does not, and what E44 must re-verify.
- [ ] Demoed to the Owner at a Sprint Review with explicit acceptance recorded.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E29` (OMS core and order state machine - the matcher and demo routing reuse it rather than reimplementing it) and `E26` (replay engine - supplies recorded book and trade events on the shared bus), per the roadmap dependency graph `E29 --> E38`, `E26 --> E38`.

E42 lands a full sprint before E38's consuming children (S19), so the buffer is one sprint.
- `blocked_by: E41` (journal & analytics, S18-S19) - E41 owns the journal/analytics data layer and the CMP-167/CMP-168 chart components E38-S05 composes, and E41's default query filter implements the simulated-exclusion rule. **E41 runs in the same S18-S19 window as E38, so this dependency is pinned at ticket level, not epic level:** E38-S05 (S19) is blocked by `E41-T01` (journal module, migrations, read API) and `E41-T03` (analytics aggregation service), both scheduled **Sprint 18**, giving one sprint of buffer. No E38 child depends on an E41 ticket scheduled in S19. If E41-T01/T03 slip out of S18, E38-S05 is the only child at risk; its fallback is to ship labelling plus the SCR-099 drawer against the matcher's own result payload and defer the journal-composed analytics view to E49.
- **Downstream:** `E38 --> E44` (live-enablement gating) - E38's parity report, capability matrix and isolation middleware are E44's evidence base and enforcement layer.

## Agent guidance

How to pick up work in this epic when multiple agents are running in parallel:

**Dependency order.** Work tickets in `blocked_by` order; a ticket is not pickable until every key in its `blocked_by` list is Done. Design (`-D*`) and spike (`-K*`) tickets generally gate the technical (`-T*`) and story (`-S*`) tickets that consume their output — check each ticket's `blocked_by` field, do not assume numeric or alphabetic order implies dependency order.

**Parallel lanes.** Tickets with disjoint `component` values and no shared `blocked_by` edge can run concurrently. QA (`-Q*`) and security (`-X*`) tickets typically depend on the corresponding `-S*`/`-T*` ticket being Done, so they are the last lane per feature slice, not a separate epic-wide phase.

**Shared interfaces to agree first.** Before two agents touch the same contract (API/WS schema, DB table, or statechart) concurrently, the one opening the PR first must land the contract change (OpenAPI/WS schema/migration) and regenerate `packages/protocol`; the second agent rebases on it rather than proposing a second incompatible shape. Statechart JSON under `machines/` is single-owner per PR — check open PRs touching the same `machines/<name>.machine.json` before starting a `statechart`-labelled ticket.

title: UX research: how traders tell demo from live and trust simulated fills
body:
## Context
E38 ships the two surfaces where a mistake is unrecoverable: the environment switch (SCR-074) and the permanent demo/live indication (SCR-075), plus three surfaces where a *misread* is nearly as damaging - the simulated-fill results drawer (SCR-099), the parity report (SCR-137) and the paper-balance reset (SCR-079).

`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` section 21 US-PAPER-002 demands that switching is 'deliberate and unmistakable'; US-PAPER-004 demands that simulated positions are 'visually marked as simulated everywhere'; US-PAPER-005 demands paper results never aggregate into live statistics. Those are research questions before they are visual questions: what do users actually look at before pressing submit, and do they discount simulated results appropriately or over-trust them?

This ticket is the research pass that de-risks D02-D04 and runs two sprints ahead of the consuming stories (design-ahead rule, `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` Team & cadence).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Moderated sessions with the Owner and 2 account managers (personas `docs/plan/10-personas.md` owner-trader, account manager), 45 min each, run against the R2 build plus clickable stubs.
- Research questions:
  1. Before submitting an order, which chrome element (if any) is consulted to confirm the environment? Test by asking participants to state the environment at unprompted moments.
  2. Does a single global band (CMP-074 EnvBanner) suffice, or is the per-panel badge (CMP-075 EnvBadgeLocal) load-bearing when a panel is floated/maximised?
  3. What confirmation friction is acceptable on the demo-to-live switch (typed phrase + step-up per SCR-074) before users start defeating it?
  4. How do users interpret simulated P&L from the paper matcher - do they treat it as achievable, and what framing (per SCR-099's 'simulated' checklist) corrects over-trust?
  5. What do users expect 'reset paper balance' (US-PAPER-006) to destroy, and do they expect live data to be touched?
  6. Would a parity report (US-PAPER-008) be read proactively or only after a surprise, and what does 'last verified' need to say to be trusted?
- Greyscale/colour-vision pre-test of demo vs live differentiation (deuteranopia, protanopia, tritanopia simulations) - required because `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-075 forbids colour-only encoding.
- Deliverable: research report in `docs/design/research/E38-paper-parity.md` with findings, verbatims, a prioritised implications list mapped to SCR-074/075/079/099/122/137, and any risk raised into `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md`.

## Out of scope
- Visual design of any screen (that is D02-D04).
- Rule-editor, order-ticket or DOM research (E30/E31/E36/E37 own theirs).
- Quantitative A/B testing - the population is 3-5 users; findings are qualitative by design.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Research executed and reported
  Given 3 participants covering the owner and manager personas
  When all sessions are complete
  Then a report exists at docs/design/research/E38-paper-parity.md answering all six research questions with evidence

Scenario: Environment-recall finding is measured, not asserted
  Given each participant is interrupted at 3 unprompted moments per session
  When asked to state the current trading environment
  Then the recall rate is recorded per chrome treatment and drives an explicit recommendation on whether per-panel badges are mandatory

Scenario: Colour-independence validated
  Given the candidate demo and live treatments
  When each is rendered in greyscale and in the three colour-vision simulations
  Then any treatment that becomes ambiguous is rejected in the report and not carried into D02

Scenario: Over-trust of simulated results surfaced
  Given participants are shown a simulated results drawer with a strong equity curve
  When asked what they would size their next live trade at
  Then any evidence of over-trust is recorded and converted into a concrete framing requirement for SCR-099
```

## Technical notes / design
- Sessions recorded (with consent) and stored on the project's private research drive, not in the repo; the repo holds only the anonymised report.
- Stimuli: R2 build with a Figma-prototype overlay for the switch modal; do not use production credentials - use `CV_ENV=dev` seeds (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` seeds section) so no real key or balance is on screen.

- Threat: research recordings could capture API key material or real balances. Control: run against `CV_ENV=dev` seed data only (fake encrypted keys per `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md`); no live or funded demo account on screen. Data classification: internal; recordings confidential and not committed.
- No `security` review label required.

N/A - no runtime component. Findings that imply telemetry (e.g. 'count environment mis-reads') are filed as follow-up tickets against E38-T02.

title: Hi-fi design: parity report, paper fidelity panel, reset and eligibility
body:
## Context
Three smaller surfaces round out E38 and all are 'honesty' surfaces: the environment parity report (US-PAPER-008, on SCR-137 Admin security centre and linked from SCR-074), the admin **paper fidelity** panel showing the nightly paper-vs-demo divergence metrics (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 12.5), the paper-balance reset on SCR-079 (US-PAPER-006), and the demo/live eligibility control on SCR-122 (US-PAPER-007).

They are grouped into one design ticket because they share a pattern language (admin tables, destructive confirmation, disabled-with-reason) and the same reviewer, and none is big enough to justify its own.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-137 Admin: security centre** - an 'Environment parity' section: table of known demo-vs-live differences with columns difference, area, source, last verified, status; a 'needs re-verification' treatment for items older than 90 days; a 'candidate parity item' inbox fed by runtime-detected demo-only failures. Components: CMP-028, CMP-036, CMP-050, CMP-087, CMP-093, CMP-175, CMP-178.
- **Admin paper fidelity panel** - the nightly divergence report: mean and p95 slippage difference, fill-rate difference for resting limits, fee difference, with the defect threshold (p95 slippage >1 tick or fill-rate >10 pp) drawn as an explicit breach state. Reuses CMP-178 SystemHealthTile and CMP-049 Table.
- **SCR-079 Account detail drawer (trading side)** - the 'Reset paper balance' control: starting-balance input, the warning when open paper positions exist, the explicit confirmation, and the **hidden-entirely-in-live** treatment (US-PAPER-006 requires hidden, not merely disabled).
- **SCR-122 Admin: user detail / edit** - demo/live eligibility control: demo-only vs live-enabled, the reason shown when Live is disabled for a manager, the acknowledgement-at-next-sign-in pattern on promotion, and the reduce-only state after revocation while positions are open.
- Empty, loading, error and RBAC-denied states for each.
- Design-system: reuse only; any new pattern raised as a contribution ticket.

## Out of scope
- The switcher and global chrome (E38-D02).
- Replay simulated-results drawer (E38-D04).
- The wider admin screens (E42 owns SCR-122's and SCR-137's overall structure; this ticket designs only the E38 sections inside them).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Parity report communicates freshness
  Given a parity item last verified 95 days ago
  When the SCR-137 parity section is reviewed
  Then a distinct 'needs re-verification' state is drawn, using text plus icon, not colour alone

Scenario: Reset is hidden in live
  Given the environment is LIVE
  When the SCR-079 frames are reviewed
  Then the reset control is absent from the drawer entirely, and a note states it must not render as a disabled control

Scenario: Destructive reset is guarded
  Given open paper positions exist
  When the user initiates a reset
  Then a confirmation is drawn that names the count of positions and orders to be discarded and requires an explicit confirm

Scenario: Revocation with open positions is designed
  Given a manager's live access is revoked while they hold live positions
  When the SCR-122 frames are reviewed
  Then a reduce-only state is drawn with copy explaining existing positions remain manageable and new entries are refused

Scenario: Fidelity breach is unmissable
  Given the nightly divergence job reports p95 slippage divergence above one tick
  When the fidelity panel is reviewed
  Then a breach state is drawn that states the threshold, the measured value and the resulting action (a defect ticket is opened)
```

## Technical notes / design

title: Spike: enumerate real Bybit demo-vs-live behavioural differences
body:
## Context
US-PAPER-008 requires a parity report 'generated from a maintained data file plus runtime observations, never hand-written prose only'. We cannot maintain a data file we have not populated, and the roadmap's R3 goal 5 is to 'prove demo/live parity gaps explicitly so R4 is a gating exercise rather than a re-architecture'.

We already know three differences from research (`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` SR-040a): demo has no WS order entry, demo has no public WS (mainnet public streams are used for market data), and demo batch orders are limited to `linear`/`option`. `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` adds a fourth (7-day demo order retention). This spike establishes the rest empirically instead of guessing, and produces the seed content for the parity data file that E38-S08 renders.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Timebox: **4 working days**, one backend engineer, against a real `api-demo.bybit.com` account created for the purpose.
- Systematically exercise, on demo and on a read-only live account, each v5 surface the product uses: order create/amend/cancel, cancel-all, batch endpoints, conditional/TP-SL orders with `tpslMode` Full/Partial, trailing stops, position mode and leverage changes, `GET /v5/account/fee-rate`, `GET /v5/market/risk-limit`, `GET /v5/order/history`, `GET /v5/position/closed-pnl`, wallet balance, and the private WS `order`/`execution`/`position`/`wallet` streams.
- For each: record supported / unsupported / behaves-differently, the exact `retCode`/`retMsg` when unsupported, the observed latency, and any field that is absent or differently populated on demo.
- Record rate-limit behaviour differences (does demo return `10006`/`10018` on the same thresholds?).
- Record how long demo order history is actually retained.
- Produce `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0026-demo-live-parity.md` recording the decision on which differences are *encoded in the capability matrix* (hard, compile-time), which are *documented in the parity report* (soft, informational), and which are *runtime-detected only*.
- Produce the first version of the parity data file (`packages/backend/cv/paper/parity_items.yaml`) with one entry per confirmed difference: id, area, description, source (doc URL or observed), severity, last_verified date.

## Out of scope
- Implementing the capability matrix (E38-T01) or the report UI (E38-S08).
- Any live order placement - the live account used is read-only and unfunded.
- Non-USDT-perp product lines (spot, options, inverse) - out of product scope.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every used v5 surface is classified
  Given the list of Bybit v5 endpoints and WS topics this product calls
  When the spike completes
  Then each has a recorded demo classification of supported, unsupported or behaves-differently, with evidence

Scenario: Unsupported operations have exact error signatures
  Given an operation unsupported on demo
  When it is attempted
  Then the observed retCode and retMsg are recorded verbatim, so E38-S01 can map them to a plain-language refusal rather than a generic failure

Scenario: The decision is recorded as an ADR
  When the spike completes
  Then ADR-0016 exists stating which differences are hard capability-matrix entries and which are informational parity items, with rationale

Scenario: The parity data file is seeded
  When the spike completes
  Then parity_items.yaml contains at least the four already-known differences plus every newly discovered one, each with a last_verified date

Scenario: A discovery that invalidates a design escalates
  Given a difference is found that breaks an existing E29/E32/E33 design assumption
  Then a risk entry is added to docs/plan/32-risk-register.md and the owning epic is notified before the spike closes
```

## Technical notes / design
- Use a scripted harness under `packages/backend/tests/manual/demo_probe.py` so the probe is repeatable later as the re-verification mechanism for US-PAPER-008's 90-day staleness rule - this is deliberately not throwaway.
- The harness reads credentials only through the envelope-encrypted store (SR-004: never from env vars or config files).
- Probe results are written as machine-readable YAML, not prose, so the parity file can be diffed on each re-run.
- Classify each difference against `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` SR-040a: anything that could cause a *silent* wrong-transport or dual-dispatch is a hard capability-matrix entry, not a documentation note.

## Test plan
- Not production code beyond the reusable probe harness; the harness itself gets unit tests for its result-parsing and YAML emission.
- The probe must be runnable in CI against recorded fixtures (`CV_FEED=synthetic`) to verify the harness without credentials - SR-140 forbids demo credentials in CI.

## Security notes
- Threat: a probe script leaking credentials into logs or the repo. Controls: credentials from the encrypted store only (SR-004), output redaction per the standard redaction rules (SR-146), the probe's YAML output asserted to contain no key-shaped strings before commit.
- Threat (W9, `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`): code assuming WS order entry exists on demo. This spike's output is the evidence base for making that unreachable by construction.
- Data classification: the demo account holds no real funds; its keys are still secrets and are handled identically to live keys.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no UI.

## Performance notes
- Record observed demo REST latency per endpoint so budget #4 (order submit to ack p95 <300 ms on demo, a hard R3 gate in `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`) can be assessed against reality before the stories commit to it.

## Observability
- The probe emits a structured summary suitable for later scheduling as the nightly/quarterly re-verification job feeding the parity report's `last_verified` field.

title: Automate the E38 end-to-end suite in Playwright web and Electron

## Context
The R3 quality gate requires Playwright coverage across web and Electron (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` section 7.4). E38's most important behaviours are cross-cutting and stateful - a switch that must tear down and rebuild every subscription, a badge that must appear on every panel including floating windows - which is precisely the class of behaviour unit tests cannot cover.

Electron matters specifically here because detached/floating windows are separate BrowserWindows, and SCR-075 requires the band to repeat in every one of them.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Add to `tests/e2e/e38/` the following suites, each running in both the web and Electron projects:
  1. **Demo order loop**: place, partial fill, amend, cancel on demo; assert state matches the orders and positions views and that the local mirror retains history.
  2. **Environment switch**: demo to live with typed confirmation and step-up; assert phase progress is shown, order entry is blocked during the transition, every open pane re-badges, one-click trading is disarmed, and working demo orders are reported as not migrated.
  3. **Switch refusals**: without step-up, with the flag off, without eligibility, and while an algo is running - each asserting the previous environment survives intact.
  4. **Badge ubiquity**: enumerate every trading-capable panel including a floated Electron window and a maximised panel, asserting the environment appears in the visible text and in the accessible name.
  5. **Cross-environment refusal**: issue a crafted API request from the browser context targeting a live account from a demo session; assert 403, no state change and an audit row visible in the security centre.
  6. **Paper reset**: reset with open positions, confirm counts, assert the control is absent in live.
  7. **Simulated results**: run a short replay with the paper matcher, open SCR-099, assert the disclosure block values, the default-off comparison, export, and promotion writing `simulated=true` journal rows.
  8. **Parity report**: view the report, trigger a demo-only failure, assert a candidate item appears and the refusal deep-links to its row.
  9. **Eligibility**: grant, acknowledge at next sign-in, revoke with open positions and assert reduce-only.
- Wire all suites into the CI E2E job with the `CV_FEED=synthetic` profile plus recorded fixtures; cases requiring a real demo account are tagged and excluded from CI per SR-140, and run on the trading host as part of the release checklist.

## Out of scope
- Load and chaos testing (E38-Q03, E38-Q04).
- The a11y audit (E38-Q05), though these suites assert accessible names where they are functionally load-bearing.
- Other epics' E2E suites.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every mandatory plan case is automated or explicitly deferred
  Given the E38-TC case list from E38-Q01
  When the suite is complete
  Then each mandatory case is either automated with its case id referenced, or deferred with a filed automation Task

Scenario: Suites pass in both web and Electron
  Given the Playwright web and Electron projects
  When CI runs
  Then all nine suites pass in both, including the floating-window badge assertion which only Electron can exercise

Scenario: The crafted cross-environment request is genuinely blocked
  Given a demo session in the browser
  When a live-targeting request is issued directly from the page context, bypassing the UI guard
  Then the API returns 403, no order exists afterwards, and the audit row is visible in the admin security centre

Scenario: Tests fail for the right reason
  Given a deliberately introduced regression removing a per-panel badge
  When the suite runs
  Then the badge-ubiquity suite fails and names the offending panel

Scenario: No credentials in CI
  Given the CI configuration
  When the suite runs
  Then it uses synthetic feeds and fixtures only, and demo-credential-requiring cases are tagged out
```

## Technical notes / design
- Use Playwright projects to share specs across web and Electron rather than duplicating them; only the launcher differs.
- Deterministic setup: each suite seeds via the `CV_ENV=dev` seed path and tears down its own data, so suites can run in any order and in parallel.
- Avoid timing flakiness on the switch suite by asserting on the `system` WS phase frames rather than sleeping.
- Badge ubiquity is driven by a panel registry rather than a hardcoded list, so a newly added trading panel is automatically covered - a new panel without a badge should fail this suite the day it lands.
- Accessible-name assertions use Playwright's accessibility snapshot, which is also the cheapest early warning for the E38-Q05 audit.

## Test plan
- The suite is the test artefact; its own reliability is verified by 20 consecutive green runs before it becomes a required check (flake budget zero for safety-critical suites).
- Mutation check: the deliberately-introduced-regression scenario above is run once per suite to confirm each actually detects its target.

- The crafted-request suite is an automated abuse case; it complements, and does not replace, E38-X02's manual review.
- Test credentials are seed-generated fakes; SR-140 forbids real demo keys in CI and the suite configuration must make that structurally impossible (no secret referenced by the workflow).

## Accessibility notes
- Accessible-name assertions are functional here (SCR-075 requires the environment in each panel's accessible name), so they live in this suite as well as in E38-Q05.

## Performance notes
- The suite records order submit-to-ack timings as an informational artefact; a gross regression against budget #4 fails a soft assertion so it is visible before the dedicated load test runs.

## Observability
- Suites assert the presence of the expected audit events (`session.environment_switched`, `trading.environment_mismatch_rejected`, `paper.balance_reset`, `journal.simulated_import`), turning observability into a tested contract rather than a hope.

body:
## Context
Budget #4 in `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` - order submit to ack p95 <300 ms on demo - is a **hard R3 exit gate**, and E38-S01 is the story that owns the demo half of it. Budget #15 requires replay at up to 100x, which the paper matcher must not bottleneck.

The environment switch adds a budget of its own: it blocks order entry for its whole duration (SCR-074 states typically <=2 s), so a slow switch is a trading outage rather than a slow page.

## Scope / Deliverables
- k6 (or Locust) script `tests/load/e38_demo_orders.js`: sustained order submit/amend/cancel against the demo path at the per-UID rate budget, measuring submit-to-ack p50/p95/p99 separated into backend-internal and exchange RTT components (budget #4 excludes Bybit RTT from the backend-internal figure, per section 3.1).
- Paper-matcher throughput benchmark: replay a recorded BTCUSDT day through the matcher, measuring matched-events per second and asserting the 20x-faster-than-real-time requirement from E38-S03 and the 100x replay ceiling of budget #15.
- Environment-switch timing: measure the full transition (teardown, re-auth, resubscribe) at a realistic subscription count (10 symbols, multi-pane workspace), asserting p95 <=2 s and recording the per-phase breakdown so a regression is attributable.
- Memory: assert the matcher stays within budget #8 (<=300 MB per actively-recorded symbol) during a full-day replay.
- Frontend: assert an environment change does not exceed the frame budget (#1) - measure the render cost of re-badging every panel in a worst-case layout.
- Record all results in `docs/perf/results/E38.md` with the reference-hardware profile stated (section 3.1) and compare against the budget table.

## Out of scope
- Chaos and failure-injection (E38-Q04).
- Load testing other epics' paths (E34 owns fan-out load).

```gherkin
  When the load script completes
  Then submit-to-ack p95 is reported with backend-internal and exchange-RTT components separated, and compared against the 300 ms budget

Scenario: Memory stays inside budget

Scenario: Re-badging does not drop frames
  Given a worst-case layout with all trading panels open

  Then no frame exceeds the 16.6 ms budget as a direct result of re-badging
```

- Measurement methods follow `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` section 7 exactly; deviating would make the numbers incomparable with other epics' results.

title: Chaos scenarios for environment switching and paper state recovery
body:
## Context
The R3 chaos gate (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` section 7.4) requires that WS kill, backend restart and Postgres failover all resume to a correct, reconciled state. E38 adds two specifically fragile moments: the environment transition, which deliberately tears down and rebuilds every private subscription, and the paper matcher's in-memory state, which must survive a restart without inventing or losing simulated positions.

SCR-074's requirement that 'a half-switched state is never reachable' is exactly the kind of claim only fault injection can test.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Scenario 1: **backend restart mid-switch** at each phase boundary (after teardown, after re-auth, after partial resubscribe) - assert the session resolves to exactly one environment with consistent subscriptions and that the UI reflects it, never a mixed state.
- Scenario 2: **WS disconnect during a demo order's lifetime** - assert reconciliation against `GET /v5/order/realtime` restores exact state with no duplicate submission and no lost fill.
- Scenario 3: **backend restart with open simulated positions and resting simulated orders** - assert the `PaperLedger` and queue estimates recover from Postgres with no ghost orders and no duplicated fills.
- Scenario 4: **Postgres unavailable during a paper reset** - assert the transaction aborts cleanly and the pre-reset state is fully intact (E38-S06's atomicity criterion under real failure rather than an injected exception).
- Scenario 5: **audit writer unavailable during a cross-environment refusal** - assert the request still fails closed (refused), because failing open would trade an audit gap for a safety breach.
- Scenario 6: **clock skew** between backend and exchange beyond the 1000 ms incident threshold during a demo order - assert the condition is detected and surfaced rather than silently producing mis-sequenced state.
- Scenario 7: **demo private WS flapping** during a switch - assert the transition either completes or rolls back, never stalls indefinitely, and that a stall has a timeout with a stated outcome.
- Record results in `docs/chaos/results/E38.md` with the injection method for each scenario so they are repeatable each release.

## Out of scope
- Fan-out and algo chaos (E34, E33 own theirs).
- Infrastructure-level failover testing of Postgres itself (E45).
- Performance measurement (E38-Q03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: No half-switched state survives a restart
  Given the backend is killed at each phase boundary of an environment switch
  When it restarts
  Then the session resolves to exactly one environment with a consistent subscription set, and the UI reflects that environment truthfully

Scenario: Paper state recovers without ghosts
  Given open simulated positions and resting simulated orders
  When the backend restarts
  Then the ledger, positions and resting orders with their queue estimates are restored from Postgres, with no duplicated fill and no order that no longer exists

Scenario: Reset is atomic under real database failure
  Given Postgres becomes unavailable mid-reset
  When the operation fails
  Then the pre-reset balance, positions and orders are all intact and the failure is reported to the user

Scenario: Refusals fail closed without the audit writer
  Given the audit writer is unavailable
  When a cross-environment request is made
  Then it is still refused, and the audit failure is itself alerted

Scenario: A stalled switch resolves rather than hanging
  Given the demo private WS flaps during a transition
  When the configured timeout elapses
  Then the transition rolls back to the previous environment with a stated reason, and order entry is unblocked

Scenario: Clock skew is detected
  Given backend-to-exchange clock offset exceeds one second
  When a demo order is placed
  Then the condition is surfaced as an incident rather than silently accepted
```

## Technical notes / design
- Injection via the project's existing chaos harness (toxiproxy for network faults, container kill for restarts, a fault-injection hook for the audit writer), documented per scenario so the suite is repeatable by anyone.
- Each scenario asserts on **observable state after recovery**, not on log lines, so the test is about correctness rather than implementation detail.
- Phase-boundary restarts are driven by pausing at the `system` phase frames E38-S02 emits, which makes the injection points precise rather than timing-based.
- Scenarios 3 and 4 need a seeded matcher state fixture; build it once and share it with E38-Q02.

## Test plan
- The scenarios are the test artefact. Each must be demonstrated to fail against a deliberately broken build (e.g. a matcher that rebuilds state from memory only), proving the scenario has teeth.
- Run as part of the release checklist, not on every PR, given their runtime.

## Security notes
- Scenario 5 is a security-relevant chaos case: fail-closed behaviour under audit-writer failure is a control, and its verification is shared with E38-X02.
- No real credentials are used; the demo-dependent scenarios run on the trading host per SR-140.

## Accessibility notes
- Scenario 7 includes verifying the UI communicates the stalled/rolled-back state accessibly (announced, not merely visual), because a silent stall during a blocked-order-entry window is dangerous.

## Performance notes
- Record recovery times per scenario; a restart that takes minutes to rebuild matcher state is a defect even if it is eventually correct.

## Observability
- Each scenario asserts that the expected alert fires (WS disconnect with open orders, audit-writer failure, clock skew incident) - verifying the alerting path at the same time as the recovery path.

## Context

- Manual screen-reader passes with **NVDA on Windows** (the primary target given the Electron shell) and a secondary pass with the platform reader in the browser build: full keyboard-only operation of the switch flow, the reset confirmation, the results drawer and the parity table.
- Verify against the E38-D05 annotation layer specifically: the band is announced on demand but does not re-announce per panel render; the post-switch banner announces once assertively; focus moves into and returns from every dialog; the typed-confirm error is announced and associated.
- Colour-independence verification on the built app: greyscale plus deuteranopia, protanopia and tritanopia simulations for the environment treatments and the simulated badge.
- Contrast re-measurement on the built app against the D05 recorded values.
- Reduced-motion verification: the chrome transition degrades to an instant swap.
- File every finding as a Bug with the WCAG success criterion referenced; blocking findings prevent epic sign-off.

## Out of scope
- Design-time annotation review (E38-D05, already done).
- Design QA of visual fidelity (E38-D07).
- Auditing other epics' panels, except to confirm the E38 badge they host is accessible.

```gherkin

  Given every E38 surface and state
  When axe-core runs
  Then there are zero violations, and the checks run on every PR rather than only during this audit

Scenario: The switch is fully keyboard operable
  Given a keyboard-only user with a screen reader
  When they switch environments
  Then the entire path from band to typed confirmation to step-up to completion is operable, with visible focus at every step and the outcome announced

Scenario: No announcement storm from repeated badges
  Given a workspace with many trading panels
  When a panel re-renders
  Then the environment is not re-announced for each panel

Scenario: Destructive counts are announced
  Given a reset with open positions
  When the confirmation opens
  Then the number of positions and orders to be discarded is announced, and focus does not default to the destructive button

Scenario: Charts have usable table alternatives
  Given the SCR-099 equity curve and R distribution
  When navigating with a screen reader only

Scenario: Environment survives colour-vision simulation on the built app

  When rendered in greyscale and the three colour-vision simulations
```

title: Trade Bybit demo through the same code paths as live
body:
## Context
US-PAPER-001 (Must) is the foundation of the whole R3 train: every order in R3 executes against Bybit demo. Its NFR is the demanding part - 'identical code paths as live except host and key selection; contract tests run against both environments'. If demo needs its own branch in the OMS, R4's live enablement becomes a re-architecture instead of a gate flip (roadmap section 7.1 goal 5).

E38-T01 gave us the capability record and host routing. This story proves the loop end to end: a demo order behaves, looks and is recorded exactly as a live one would, the demo private WS drives the UI identically, and an operation demo cannot do is refused in plain language rather than failing obscurely.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Wire the demo environment through the existing OMS order path (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 8 state machine): submit via REST to `api-demo.bybit.com` with `orderLinkId` idempotency, accept the REST response as *acceptance only*, and take order state from the demo **private WS** `order`/`execution`/`position`/`wallet` streams, exactly as live does.
- Demo private WS client lifecycle: connect, authenticate, subscribe, heartbeat, reconnect with resubscribe, and the reconciliation loop against `GET /v5/order/realtime` and `/v5/position/list` on reconnect and on a timer - reusing E29's implementation, not a copy.
- Map `CapabilityUnsupported` (E38-T01) and demo-specific exchange errors to a plain-language refusal carrying the operation, the reason and the parity item id, surfaced through the standard RFC 9457 problem body.
- Ensure every persisted row carries the right environment: `orders.environment`, `positions`, `order_events.source`, and `is_paper=false` for demo (demo is a real matching engine - `is_paper` is orthogonal per `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 1.2).

## Out of scope
- The local paper matcher (E38-S03) - demo is a real exchange engine, not a simulation.
- The environment switch UX (E38-S02, E38-S04).
- Live order entry, which remains gated off until R4/E44.

```gherkin
Scenario: Demo order behaves as a live order
  Given the session is in Demo with a demo-bound account
  When an order is submitted
  Then it is sent to the api-demo host and appears in positions exactly as a live order would, with the same fields populated

Scenario: Demo private stream drives the UI
  Given a demo account with an open order
  When the order fills at the exchange
  Then order, execution, position and wallet updates arrive over the demo private WS and drive state identically to live, with the WS stream and not the REST ack as the source of truth

Scenario: Demo-only limitation is refused plainly
  Given an operation unsupported in demo
  When it is attempted
  Then it is refused with the limitation stated in plain language and a parity item id, never a generic or obscure failure

Scenario: Identical code paths, proven
  Given the OMS contract-test suite
  When it is executed against demo and against live configuration
  Then the only configuration difference is host and key selection, and both runs produce identical assertions

Scenario: Local history outlives exchange retention
  Given demo orders older than the exchange's retention window
  When the local order history is queried
  Then the records are still present and complete, sourced from the local mirror

Scenario: Reconnect reconciles rather than duplicates
  Given the demo private WS drops mid-order
  When it reconnects
  Then reconciliation against order/realtime restores exact state with no duplicated order and no lost fill
```

title: Switch session environment safely with step-up and full resubscription
body:
## Context
US-PAPER-002 (Must) requires switching to be 'deliberate and unmistakable'. `POST /session/environment` in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` already specifies the contract: switching *to* `live` requires an elevated session (`/auth/step-up`) and the `live_trading` feature flag, else `403 step_up_required` or `403 live_trading_disabled`; the switch is audited and broadcast on the `system` WS topic so every pane re-badges consistently.

SCR-074 adds the operational requirement that makes this non-trivial: on success the client tears down and re-establishes **every** private subscription, order entry is blocked for the whole transition, and 'a half-switched state is never reachable'.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Implement `POST /session/environment` per the OpenAPI contract: validate the target environment is in the caller's `allowed_environments`; for `live`, require an elevated session within the last 15 minutes and the `live_trading` flag on; otherwise return the specified 403 problem.
- Refuse the switch while the session has **in-flight state that would be orphaned**: a running emulated algo (E33), an in-flight trade group (E34), or a pending order submission - returning a refusal that names the specific blocker (the SCR-074 design sign-off checklist requires this state to exist).
- Orchestrate the transition server-side as an ordered, non-interleavable sequence: block order entry for the session, close private subscriptions for the old environment, re-derive the session's account scope and permissions for the new environment, open private subscriptions for the new environment, unblock. Any failure rolls back to the previous environment intact - never a partial state.
- Broadcast the resulting environment on the `system` WS topic so every open pane and every other tab re-badges; include the transition phases so the UI can show the progress states SCR-074 specifies.
- Audit `session.environment_switched` at high severity with from, to, user, session, and outcome; also audit refusals.
- On switching to live, disarm one-click trading for the session (US-PAPER-002: 'one-click trading is disarmed on switch'), independently of the arm timeout in `POST /settings/arm`.
- Working orders in the previous environment are **not** migrated and remain untouched; the response includes their count so the UI can state it.

## Out of scope
- The switch UI (E38-S04).
- The step-up/2FA mechanism itself (E09).
- The `live_trading` flag's administration (E42) and the R4 live-enablement gate (E44) - this story only reads the flag.
- Per-user eligibility grants (E38-S07).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Switching to live requires step-up and the flag
  Given a session that has not been elevated in the last 15 minutes
  When a switch to live is requested
  Then the response is 403 step_up_required, the environment is unchanged, and the refusal is audited

Scenario: Live trading disabled blocks the switch
  Given the live_trading feature flag is off
  And the session is elevated
  When a switch to live is requested
  Then the response is 403 live_trading_disabled and the environment is unchanged

Scenario: Successful switch resubscribes everything
  Given a demo session with open private subscriptions
  When a valid switch to live is performed
  Then private subscriptions for demo are closed before any live subscription opens, the new environment is broadcast on the system topic, and order entry is blocked for the whole transition

Scenario: A half-switched state is never reachable
  Given the resubscription step fails midway
  When the transition aborts
  Then the session is left fully on the previous environment with its subscriptions restored, and the failure reason is returned and audited

Scenario: Switching is blocked by in-flight activity
  Given a running emulated algo or an in-flight trade group
  When a switch is requested
  Then it is refused with the specific blocker named, and no subscription is disturbed

Scenario: One-click trading is disarmed on switch to live
  Given one-click trading is armed in demo
  When the session switches to live
  Then the armed state is cleared and a new explicit arm is required

Scenario: No hotkey path exists
  Given the hotkey configuration surface
  When all bindable actions are enumerated
  Then no binding can invoke the environment switch
```

## Technical notes / design
- The transition is guarded by a per-session lock; concurrent switch requests return `409` rather than interleaving.
- Phases are emitted as `system` topic frames (`closing_subscriptions`, `reauthenticating`, `resubscribing`, `switched`) matching the SCR-074 progress states, so the UI is not guessing.
- Rollback is structured as a compensating step per completed phase, executed in reverse order; a test injects failure at each phase boundary.
- Account scope re-derivation reuses E09's session resolution rather than reimplementing it; the new scope must exclude every account whose `env` differs from the new environment.
- The 'blocked by in-flight activity' check queries the algo and trade-group registries; the blocker list is returned as structured data, not a prose string, so the UI can render each blocker with a link.

## Test plan
- Unit: authorisation matrix over (target env, elevated?, flag state, allowed_environments) with the exact expected problem code for every cell.
- Unit: rollback correctness with failure injected at each phase.
- Unit: blocker detection for running algo, in-flight group and pending submission.
- Contract: response and error shapes against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`; `system` frame shape against `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`.
- Integration: full switch against a seeded two-environment account set, asserting subscription teardown/setup ordering from the WS server's connection log.
- Integration: concurrent switch requests yield exactly one switch and one 409.
- E2E (feeds E38-Q02): switch from demo to live with step-up on staging, asserting every open pane re-badges.
- Coverage target: >=90% (safety-critical path).

## Security notes
- This endpoint is the single gateway to live. Threats: elevation of privilege (switching without step-up), tampering (racing two switches into a mixed state), repudiation (an unaudited switch), denial of service (switch-flapping to disrupt subscriptions).
- Controls: step-up requirement (SR-043-adjacent arming semantics), feature-flag gate, per-session lock, high-severity audit on success **and** refusal, rate-limit on the endpoint.
- The refusal message for a missing grant must not reveal other users' grants (information disclosure).
- `security` label mandatory; abuse-case checks are covered by E38-X02.

## Accessibility notes
- The phase broadcasts exist so the UI can announce progress assertively (SCR-074 a11y note: the environment change is announced assertively and the chrome change is accompanied by a text badge change). The API must therefore emit phases promptly, not only a final result.

## Performance notes
- The whole transition should typically complete in <=2 s (SCR-074 performance note). Measure and record p95; the transition blocks order entry, so a slow switch is a trading outage.
- Subscription teardown/setup must not thrash the WS fan-out budget; batch the resubscribe rather than issuing one frame per topic.

## Observability
- Audit `session.environment_switched` (high severity) plus `session.environment_switch_refused` with reason.
- Metric `cv_environment_switch_duration_seconds` and `cv_environment_switch_failures_total{phase}`.
- A failed rollback is a P0 alert - it implies a possibly half-switched session.

title: Simulate fills locally with the paper matcher's queue, latency and fee models
body:
## Context
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** The paper matcher's queue/fill/fee arithmetic stays excluded, per-tick plain code (29-statechart-adoption-plan §3); only the paper account's liquidation lifecycle moves onto `B15` (`paper_account`) on `xstate-statemachine`. Net estimate unchanged.

US-PAPER-004 (Should) asks for an offline simulator so the owner can practise and develop with no exchange dependency, and so rule simulation and replay have somewhere to execute. Its NFR is the design constraint: 'simulator uses the same OMS state machine as real trading so behaviour is comparable'.

`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 12 specifies the matcher in full and is normative for this story: the `FillModelConfig`, the book-walk for market orders, the queue-position model for resting limits (including the pro-rata cancel assumption described there as 'the single most important honesty knob in the whole simulator'), latency, fees from `GET /v5/account/fee-rate`, funding as an `Execution` with `exec_type="funding"`, and margin/liquidation from real tiered risk-limit data. `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` section 3.7 names the components: `FillModel`, `QueueEstimator`, `FeeModel`, `PaperLedger`.

The point of all this detail is honesty: a simulator that ignores queue position, latency and funding lies, and a lying simulator is worse than none because it manufactures confidence (risk R12).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Implement module **M16 Paper Matcher** in `packages/backend/cv/paper/`: `FillModel`, `QueueEstimator`, `FeeModel`, `PaperLedger`, exposing the **same interface as the exchange adapter** (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 14) so the OMS routes to it without knowing it is a simulation.
- `FillModelConfig` exactly as specified in section 12.1 (all fields, same defaults: `mode=book_walk`, `use_queue_position=True`, `prob_fill_on_touch=0.35`, `latency_submit_ms=60`, `latency_cancel_ms=60`, `latency_market_data_ms=30`, `max_book_levels=200`, `reject_if_book_exhausted=True`, `apply_funding=True`).
- Market orders: walk the opposite side of the live/replayed L2 book from best, one `Execution` per level consumed, volume-weighted average price; `INSUFFICIENT_LIQUIDITY` rejection when the book is exhausted and `reject_if_book_exhausted` is set, else fill at last level plus `slippage_floor_ticks`.
- Limit orders: crossing fills as taker capped at the limit price with the remainder resting; `post_only` that would cross is **rejected**, as the exchange does.
- Resting limits with queue position: snapshot same-side displayed size as `queue_ahead`; decrement by same-side prints at the level; fill only past a cleared queue; clear the estimate when price moves away; re-cap on return; and on a level shrinking without a print, apply the pro-rata assumption `queue_ahead *= new_level_size / old_level_size`.
- Latency: orders become live at `submit_ts + latency_submit_ms`, cancels take effect at `cancel_ts + latency_cancel_ms` (so a cancel can lose the race), decision market data delayed by `latency_market_data_ms`.
- Fees from `GET /v5/account/fee-rate` cached 24 h, `is_maker` true only for a resting limit filled by an incoming aggressor, negative maker rates supported, `fee_estimated=True` marking when defaults (maker 2 bps / taker 5.5 bps) are used.
- Funding at each `next_funding_time` using the real rate and `instrument.funding_interval_min` (never assumed 8 h), recorded as an `Execution` with `exec_type="funding"`, `qty=0`.
- Margin, liquidation and the `adl_risk_proxy` per section 12.4, using fetched `GET /v5/market/risk-limit` tiers, never hardcoded.
- `PaperLedger` persists positions, wallet and realised/unrealised PnL in Postgres with the **identical schema to live accounts** (`is_paper=true` on the rows) so every downstream view is account-type agnostic.
- Hard interlock: the matcher has **no network transport**; a structural test asserts `cv/paper/` imports no HTTP or WS client.
- Implement the paper account's liquidation lifecycle as `B15` (`paper_account`) in `statechart/machines/B15.paper_account.machine.json` (committed by E50-S02, hash-locked). Do not hand-write the state enum or transition table for liquidation.
- Build it only through `statechart.factory.build('paper_account', lane=…)`, and restore it only through `statechart.persistence.restore`.
- Write guards, actions and services in `statechart/bindings/b15_paper_account.py` as a `MachineLogic`. Everything is `async def`, and services are idempotent under re-entry.
- Add `tests/xstate_contract/test_b15_paper_account.py`, which becomes a member of the blocking gate.
- All sends go through `statechart.gateway`.
- The `FillModel`/`QueueEstimator`/`FeeModel`/`PaperLedger` matcher core itself is excluded (§3) and stays plain code — do not attempt to model queue position or fill arithmetic as chart states.


## Out of scope
- The SCR-099 results UI (E38-S05) and the simulated labelling system it renders.
- The nightly divergence job (E38-S05's dependency is only the display; the job itself is E38-T03).
- Bybit demo routing (E38-S01) - demo is a real engine, this is the local one.
- Backtesting over historical bars as a product feature (E26 replay owns the data source; this is the fill engine it drives).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Limit fills when the book and prints would have filled it
  Given simulator mode against live market data
  When a limit order is placed and the level trades through after the estimated queue ahead is consumed
  Then it fills, applying the configured latency and slippage model, with one Execution per consuming print

Scenario: Market order walks the book rather than filling at one price
  Given a market order larger than the best level
  When it is matched
  Then it produces one Execution per level consumed and an average price equal to the volume-weighted result

Scenario: Book exhaustion rejects rather than inventing liquidity
  Given reject_if_book_exhausted is true and the order exceeds total displayed depth
  When it is matched
  Then the remainder is rejected with INSUFFICIENT_LIQUIDITY

Scenario: post_only that would cross is rejected
  Given a post_only limit priced through the opposite best
  When it is submitted
  Then it is rejected exactly as the exchange would reject it

Scenario: A cancel can lose the race
  Given a resting order about to be filled and a cancel submitted within the cancel latency window
  When the fill occurs before cancel_ts plus latency_cancel_ms
  Then the order fills and the cancel is rejected as too late

Scenario: Queue shrinkage is treated conservatively
  Given a level that shrinks without any trade print
  When the queue estimate is updated
  Then queue_ahead is reduced only pro rata to the level size change, never to zero

Scenario: Funding is a real P&L component
  Given an open simulated position held across a funding timestamp
  When funding settles
  Then an Execution with exec_type funding and qty zero is written with the signed payment using the real rate and the instrument's funding interval

Scenario: Model disclosure is machine-readable
  Given a completed simulated session
  When its results are requested
  Then the applied FillModelConfig is returned alongside them so the panel can state queue position, latency, slippage and fee assumptions

Scenario: The simulator can never place an exchange order
  Given simulator mode
  When any order is submitted
  Then no network call is made, and a structural test asserts the paper package imports no HTTP or WS client

Scenario: Simulated state is marked everywhere
  Given simulated orders, executions and positions
  When they are persisted and published
  Then every row and every WS frame carries is_paper true
```

## Technical notes / design
- The matcher consumes the **same event bus** the live path uses (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 13: replay re-emits recorded events onto the same bus with the same types), so it works identically over live and replayed data without a second code path.
- Determinism is a requirement, not a nicety: given the same event sequence and config, the matcher must produce byte-identical executions, because rule simulation (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 11) and R3 exit criterion 6 depend on deterministic replay. Seed any randomness explicitly from the session id.
- All monetary arithmetic uses `Decimal` with the instrument's tick/lot precision; fees quantized to 8 dp `ROUND_HALF_UP` as specified.
- The matcher is per paper account, in-memory plus Postgres (`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` C11), and must be restart-safe: ledger state is recoverable from Postgres, resting orders are re-registered with their persisted `queue_ahead`.
- `is_paper` is orthogonal to `environment` - a paper fill still belongs to a real environment (demo, or live when replaying live-recorded data). Do not collapse them (`docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` section 13.1 comment).
- Normative contract: `28-statechart-catalogue.md` §B15.1-.6. Mandatory config: 29-statechart-adoption-plan §1.2. The matcher core (fills, queue, fees) is a hot-path exclusion (29 §3) and stays plain code; only account liquidation state is chart-derived.


## Test plan
- Unit: queue estimator - a dedicated table-driven suite covering trade-through, partial consumption, price-away clearing, re-cap on return, and the pro-rata cancel case; this is the highest-value test set in the story.
- Unit: book walk with exact expected VWAP over a fixture book; exhaustion; `slippage_floor_ticks` behaviour.
- Unit: latency race (cancel wins / cancel loses) at the boundary millisecond.
- Unit: fee computation incl. maker rebate, estimated-fee marking, and cache expiry.
- Unit: funding sign convention for long and short, non-8h intervals.
- Unit: liquidation tier maths against fixture risk-limit data.
- Property test: total simulated fill quantity never exceeds available displayed liquidity within the configured level cap.
- Determinism test: the same recorded window replayed twice yields identical execution streams (supports R3 exit criterion 6).
- Integration: a full replay session through E26 producing simulated positions and a closed ledger, restart-recovered mid-session.
- Perf: 1 hour of recorded BTCUSDT ticks matched faster than real time by at least 20x, to support replay speeds.
- Coverage target: >=90% on `cv/paper/` (engine package, local policy above the 85% floor).
- pure-API unit tests of the b15 binding module with a `SimulatedClock`
- contract-suite membership (`test_b15_paper_account.py`), covering both spellings and every §B15.6 invariant
- a snapshot round-trip (persist→restore) at every quiescence point the liquidation lifecycle introduces, plus a refused restore on a hash or HMAC mismatch


## Security notes
- Threat: the simulator reaching the network and placing a real order. Control: the structural no-transport test plus routing that only reaches the matcher for `is_paper` accounts; this is the story's single most important control and is re-checked in E38-X02.
- Threat (R12): simulated results being mistaken for achievable results. Control: mandatory model disclosure returned with every result set, rendered by E38-S05.
- Fee-rate calls use the account's real credentials through the vault; no new credential path is introduced.
- Data classification: financial simulation data, internal.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - backend engine. The disclosure payload it emits is what makes E38-S05's accessible disclosure block possible.

## Performance notes
- Matching must sustain replay at up to 100x (budget #15) without becoming the bottleneck; profile the queue estimator, which runs per print per resting order.
- Memory: the matcher holds at most `max_book_levels` (200) per symbol plus resting orders; assert it stays inside the per-symbol backend memory budget #8 (<=300 MB).

## Observability
- Metrics: `cv_paper_fills_total{mode}`, `cv_paper_rejections_total{reason}`, `cv_paper_match_latency_seconds`, `cv_paper_queue_estimate_resets_total`.
- Every simulated execution logs its `queue_ahead` at fill time, which is what makes the divergence job (E38-T03) able to attribute differences.
