title: Show demo/live chrome everywhere and switch environments from the shell
body:
## Context
SCR-075 is called 'the single most safety-critical visual element in the app' in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`, and US-PAPER-002's second scenario requires that 'a persistent accent and a text badge mark every trading-capable surface, and the badge is never colour-only'. US-PAPER-003 requires every trading-capable view to reflect and enforce the current environment.

This story builds SCR-074 (the switcher) and SCR-075 (the permanent chrome) against the signed-off designs from E38-D06 and the backend from E38-S02/T02.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **CMP-074 EnvBanner**: persistent global band in the app shell (SCR-010), rendering `DEMO`/`LIVE` as text plus icon plus pattern, never colour alone; `role="status"` region read early in document order; never scrolled away and never covered by a modal. The demo variant states 'Demo uses Bybit's demo matching engine - REST order entry only, no private WS order entry.'
- **CMP-075 EnvBadgeLocal**: repeated in the header of every trading-capable panel - order ticket (CMP-107), group ticket, DOM ladder, positions grid, algo monitor and the chart-trading overlay - and repeated in every floating window. `role="img"` with a static label so it does not re-announce on each panel re-render.
- Every trading panel's accessible name includes the environment ('Order ticket - LIVE - Main') per SCR-075.
- **SCR-074 switcher modal**: opened only by clicking the band (no hotkey may be bound - assert this in the hotkey registry), listing live accounts available, stating that working orders in the current environment stay there and are not migrated, requiring the typed confirmation phrase plus step-up, and rendering all catalogued states: switching (with the phase progress from E38-S02's `system` frames), switched (10 s full-width confirmation banner), failed (stays on the previous environment with the reason), not permitted, and blocked-by-in-flight-activity with the blocker list.
- **CMP-139 EnvironmentAwareOrderGuard**: wrap the order ticket and DOM click-to-trade handlers so a mismatch renders the wrapped control disabled-with-reason rather than silently rerouting; this is defence in depth over E38-T02's server check.
- Order confirmation copy restates the environment ('You are about to send a **LIVE** order') per SCR-075.
- A single shared environment store subscription feeds every badge; the band does not remount on route change.

## Out of scope
- The backend switch endpoint (E38-S02) and isolation middleware (E38-T02).
- Parity report, reset, eligibility and simulated-results surfaces (S05-S08).
- The step-up modal (E09).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Environment is visible on every trading-capable surface
  Given any trading panel including a floated or maximised one
  When it is rendered
  Then it shows the environment badge in its header and includes the environment in its accessible name

Scenario: Switching is deliberate
  Given the session is in Demo
  When the user attempts to reach Live
  Then the only path is clicking the band, typing the confirmation phrase and passing step-up, and no hotkey binding can invoke it

Scenario: One-click trading is disarmed on switch
  Given one-click trading is armed
  When the environment switches
  Then the UI reflects the disarmed state returned by the server and no one-click action is operable until re-armed

Scenario: The transition blocks order entry
  Given a switch is in progress
  When the user attempts to submit an order
  Then every order-entry control is disabled with the transition stated, and the phase progress is shown and announced

Scenario: A failed switch leaves the previous environment intact
  Given the server returns a failure mid-transition
  When the modal handles it
  Then the previous environment's chrome is restored unchanged and the failure reason is displayed

Scenario: Not-permitted state is explanatory but not disclosing
  Given a manager without live access
  When they open the switcher
  Then the switch action is disabled with the reason that the owner has not enabled Live for their account, without naming who does have access

Scenario: Mismatched order is blocked client-side too
  Given the workspace environment context is demo and a control targets a live account
  When submission is attempted
  Then CMP-139 disables the control with a reason and no request is sent

Scenario: Distinguishable without colour
  Given the built application
  When rendered in greyscale and in three colour-vision simulations
  Then DEMO and LIVE remain unambiguous
```

## Technical notes / design
- One Zustand (or the project's chosen store) slice holds `{environment, phase, allowedEnvironments, armed}`, hydrated from `GET /auth/session` and updated from the `system` WS topic; badges subscribe with selectors so an environment change does not re-render panel bodies.
- The band lives in the shell layout above the router outlet so it never unmounts on navigation; modals render in a portal *below* the band in stacking order.
- The hotkey assertion is a unit test over the hotkey registry (`GET /settings/hotkeys` vocabulary) asserting no action id maps to the environment switch.
- All colours come from `color.env.demo` / `color.env.live` tokens; a lint rule forbids literal hex in these components.
- Phase progress consumes the `system` frames from E38-S02 rather than a client-side timer, so the UI cannot claim completion the server has not reached.
- Electron: the band must render identically in detached/floating windows, which are separate BrowserWindows - the store is synchronised across windows via the existing IPC bridge, not duplicated fetches.

## Test plan
- Unit: badge renders text for each environment; accessible name composition for each panel type.
- Unit: hotkey registry assertion (no binding reaches the switch).
- Interaction (Testing Library): typed-confirm gate - the switch button stays disabled until the exact phrase is typed; cancel restores focus to the band.
- Interaction: CMP-139 mismatch disables with reason and emits no request.
- Storybook + visual regression: Demo, Live, SwitchConfirmFlow, switching, switched, failed, not-permitted, blocked - in both themes and both densities.
- axe-core: zero violations on the shell with the band and on the open modal.
- E2E Playwright (web and Electron, feeds E38-Q02): full switch with step-up; badge presence on every trading panel; floating-window badge; band not covered by a modal.
- Coverage target: >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
- This is the user-facing half of SR-040a and the visible part of US-PAPER-003. A missing or wrong badge is a `priority/p0-critical` security-labelled defect.
- CMP-139 is defence in depth only - the test suite must include a case proving that bypassing the client guard still results in a server 403 (cross-referenced with E38-T02), so nobody is tempted to treat the client as the boundary.
- Not-permitted copy must not disclose other users' grants.
- No credential or key material is rendered on any of these surfaces.

## Accessibility notes
- WCAG 2.2 AA per the E38-D05 annotation layer: band is `role="status"` and polite; the post-switch confirmation is `role="alert"` announced once; the modal traps focus, focuses the typed-confirm field on open and returns focus to the band on close; visible focus throughout; error states announced and associated with their field.
- The environment distinction is text plus icon plus pattern (1.4.1); contrast >=4.5:1 text and >=3:1 non-text (1.4.3/1.4.11).
- Reduced-motion: the chrome transition degrades to an instant swap.
- Manual NVDA pass required; recorded on the ticket.

## Performance notes
- The band is part of the shell and must not remount on route change; verify with the React profiler.

- No regression to budget #10 (cold start <=3 s) or #9 (bundle size) - the band and badges are tiny and must stay in the initial bundle since they are safety chrome and may never be lazily loaded.

## Observability
- Client analytics: switcher opened, confirmation typed, switch confirmed, switch cancelled, switch failed (with phase).
- Verify the server-side `session.environment_switched` audit row appears after a UI-driven switch (checked in E38-D07 and E38-Q02).

title: Present simulated results with model disclosure and simulated-everywhere labels
body:
## Context
US-PAPER-004's third scenario requires that simulator positions are 'visually marked as simulated everywhere', and US-PAPER-005 requires paper results to be 'stored separately and never aggregate into live statistics, with a clear label on every view' and journaled 'with the same fields plus an environment tag'.

SCR-099's design sign-off checklist demands that every figure carries the 'simulated' framing, that fill-model assumptions are stated explicitly, and that comparison against real trades is opt-in and clearly separated. This story ships SCR-099 and the cross-cutting `is_paper` labelling designed in E38-D04.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Build **SCR-099 Replay paper-trading results** as a drawer at the end of a replay session: simulated fills, P&L, R distribution, per-trade list with entry/exit and R, the modelled slippage assumptions, export (CMP-099), and the 'these results are not a backtest guarantee' caveat. Components: CMP-049 Table, CMP-099 PrintExportBar, CMP-116 PnLBadge, CMP-167 JournalEquityCurveChart, CMP-168 JournalStatsSummaryCard.
- The **fill-model disclosure block**, rendered from the `FillModelConfig` returned by E38-S03 - queue position on/off, submit/cancel/market-data latency, slippage mode, fee source (live rate vs estimated default), funding applied - with each value shown, not merely named.
- Opt-in comparison against the same period's real trades, **off by default**, with the two series visually and textually separated and never summed into one total.
- The **simulated labelling system** applied across surfaces that render `is_paper` rows: orders blotter, positions grid, journal list, journal trade detail and analytics headers - badge in the heading and in the accessible name, not only a chip.
- Analytics exclusion: paper rows are excluded from live statistics by default with an explicit, labelled include-toggle; promoting a session to the journal writes entries flagged `simulated=true`.
- A table alternative for every chart on SCR-099, reachable by keyboard.

## Out of scope
- The matcher itself (E38-S03) and the divergence job (E38-T03).
- Journal analytics computation (E41) - this story contributes the simulated treatment and the exclusion rule that E41's queries honour.
- Replay transport controls (E26).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every figure carries simulated framing
  Given a completed replay paper session
  When the results drawer opens
  Then the word Simulated appears in the region heading and in the accessible name of every results region

Scenario: Fill-model assumptions are stated with their values
  Given the session used a specific FillModelConfig
  When the disclosure block renders
  Then queue position, submit latency, cancel latency, market-data latency, slippage mode, fee source and funding application are each shown with the value actually used

Scenario: Estimated fees are flagged
  Given the matcher fell back to default fee rates
  When results render
  Then the fee figures are marked as estimated, with the reason available

Scenario: Comparison is opt-in and separated
  Given the comparison against real trades
  When the drawer first opens
  Then comparison is off, and when enabled the simulated and real series remain separately labelled and are never aggregated into a single total

Scenario: Paper results never aggregate into live statistics
  Given a journal containing both simulated and real trades
  When live analytics are computed
  Then simulated rows are excluded by default and the include-toggle is explicit and labelled

Scenario: Every chart has a keyboard-reachable table alternative
  Given the equity curve and the R distribution
  When navigating by keyboard only
  Then a table alternative for each is reachable and readable by a screen reader

Scenario: Promotion to journal is tagged and audited
  Given the user promotes the session to the journal
  When the entries are written
  Then each is flagged simulated true and the action is audited as journal.simulated_import
```

## Technical notes / design
- Results are computed server-side at session end and fetched once (SCR-099 performance note); the drawer has a skeleton state sized to the final layout and no live subscriptions remain open.
- The simulated badge is a design-system component contributed by E38-D04, not a page-local element, so every consuming surface picks it up by upgrading the package.
- `is_paper` drives the badge; `environment` drives the env badge. The two must render distinctly - a unit test asserts a demo simulated row shows both and that neither substitutes for the other.
- Analytics exclusion is implemented as a default query filter in the journal data layer (coordinated with E41), not as a per-component filter, so a new view cannot accidentally include paper rows.
- Chart colour/series encodings must be distinguishable without colour; prefer direct labelling over a legend for the two-series comparison.
- Export reuses E41's CSV/Parquet export path with the simulated flag included as a column.

## Test plan
- Unit: disclosure block renders every `FillModelConfig` field including the estimated-fee marking.
- Unit: badge placement rules across blotter/positions/journal/analytics; simulated and environment badges coexist.
- Unit: analytics default excludes `is_paper` rows; the include-toggle changes the query, not just the display.
- Interaction: comparison toggle defaults off; enabling never merges totals.
- axe-core: zero violations on the drawer, incl. the table alternatives.
- Storybook: populated, empty (no simulated trades), loading, error, comparison-on, estimated-fees.
- E2E (feeds E38-Q02): run a short replay session with the paper matcher, open the drawer, export, promote to journal and assert the journal rows are flagged and audited.
- Coverage target: >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
- Threat R12: simulated results leaking into live performance statistics and driving real position sizing. Controls: data-layer default exclusion, mandatory labelling, audited promotion.

- Hard refusal if the target account's `env` is `live` or the account is not paper-capable - returning 403 and auditing the attempt at high severity (this is a data-destruction path pointed at the wrong account type).
- Frontend on **SCR-079**: the reset control with a starting-balance input validated against the instrument/account constraints; a warning naming the exact count of open simulated positions and resting orders that will be discarded; an explicit confirmation (CMP-044 ConfirmDialog, variant per E38-D06); and **complete absence of the control when the environment is live** - not a disabled control.
- Analytics: the new paper session id partitions results so a fresh run is not blended with the previous one; surfaced in the journal filter.

## Out of scope
- Resetting a Bybit demo account's real balance at the exchange (not possible through the API; only the local paper ledger is reset - state this in the UI copy).

Scenario: Analytics separate the runs

- Unit: atomicity - inject a failure after positions are cleared and assert full rollback.

- Contract: the new endpoint against the OpenAPI document; error registry entry for the refusal code.
- Integration: reset with open positions, then verify matcher state, ledger, journal record and audit row.

- This is a destructive data operation. Threats: wrong-target destruction (live account), unauthorised destruction (a manager resetting an account they merely view), repudiation.

title: Grant, revoke and acknowledge per-user demo and live eligibility
body:
## Context
US-PAPER-007 (Should) lets the owner control who may use demo and live so new managers start safely. Its NFR is precise: 'eligibility is a server-side attribute of the user-account binding'. That binding already exists as `user_account_access` (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` section 3.1.3), and the session already exposes `allowed_environments` (`docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `SessionInfo`, `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` `auth_ok`).

The hardest requirement is revocation while positions are open: existing positions must remain manageable in **reduce-only** mode while new entries are refused - a graceful degradation, not a hard cut that would trap a manager in a position they cannot close.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Persist live eligibility as a server-side attribute of the user-account binding: extend `user_account_access` (migration) with `live_enabled boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false` and `live_enabled_acknowledged_at timestamptz`, and derive `allowed_environments` for a session from the union over the user's granted accounts, intersected with the `live_trading` flag.
- Grant and revoke through the existing `PUT /users/{userId}/account-access` surface, extending `AccountAccessGrantInput` with the eligibility field; changes are audited and take effect on the next request, with existing WS subscriptions for revoked scope terminated with a `revoked` frame (reason `account_scope_changed`, `23-ws-protocol.md` §9.5), which E42-T08 delivers for that endpoint; E42-T04's contract slice S1 replaces the older `unsubscribed` wording in `22-api-openapi.yaml`.
- **Acknowledgement on promotion**: when live access is granted, the user must acknowledge the change at next sign-in before any live-targeting action is permitted; the acknowledgement is recorded and audited.
- **Revocation with open positions**: when live access is revoked while the user holds live positions, their session enters reduce-only for those accounts - amend/cancel/close are permitted, position-opening is refused with a clear reason - until the positions are flat.
- Frontend on **SCR-122 Admin: user detail / edit**: the eligibility control, the current-state display, the reason surfaced to a demo-only manager on SCR-074 ('The owner hasn't enabled Live for your account.'), the acknowledgement prompt at sign-in, and the reduce-only banner state.
- Wire `allowed_environments` into E38-T02's isolation check so eligibility is enforced at the same choke point rather than in a second place.

## Out of scope
- Role and permission administration generally (E42 owns SCR-122's structure and the RBAC matrix).
- The `live_trading` global flag (E42) and the R4 live-enablement gate (E44).
- Reduce-only enforcement mechanics in the OMS (E29/E39 own the reduce-only order path; this story sets the flag that turns it on for a user-account pair).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A demo-only manager cannot select live
  Given a manager whose grants include no live-enabled account
  When they open the environment switcher
  Then no live account is selectable and the Live switch is disabled with the reason shown

Scenario: Promotion requires acknowledgement
  Given the owner grants live access to a manager
  When that manager next signs in
  Then they must acknowledge the change before any live-targeting action is permitted, and both the grant and the acknowledgement are audited

Scenario: Revocation with open positions degrades to reduce-only
  Given a manager holds live positions
  When the owner revokes their live access
  Then existing positions remain manageable in reduce-only mode while new entries are refused with a stated reason

Scenario: Revocation with no open positions is immediate
  Given a manager holds no live positions
  When live access is revoked
  Then live-targeting requests are refused with 403 from the next request, and live subscriptions are force-closed

Scenario: Eligibility is enforced server-side, not in the UI
  Given a manager without live eligibility
  When a crafted live-targeting request is sent directly to the API
  Then it is refused with 403 and audited, independently of what the UI offered

Scenario: A manager cannot self-grant
  Given a manager with accounts:write on their own grants
  When they attempt to set live eligibility on themselves
  Then the request is refused: eligibility changes require the owner's users:write permission
```

## Technical notes / design
- Reuse the existing account-access endpoint rather than inventing an eligibility endpoint - the story's NFR explicitly places eligibility on the user-account binding, and a second surface would split the decision across two places (the same reasoning `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` gives for rejecting a `rules:arm_live` permission).
- Session `allowed_environments` derivation is cached per session and invalidated on grant change; the force-close of revoked subscriptions is the existing mechanism from `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` section 9.
- Reduce-only is expressed as a per-(user, account) flag consumed by the OMS's existing reduce-only path; it is set at revocation and cleared automatically when the account's live positions reach flat.
- Acknowledgement is a row, not a client-side dismissal: the API refuses live actions while `live_enabled_acknowledged_at` is null for a currently-granted account.
- Migration is additive with a safe default (`false`), so no existing user silently gains live access.

## Test plan
- Unit: `allowed_environments` derivation over grant combinations, incl. the `live_trading` flag being off.
- Unit: self-grant refusal; owner-only enforcement.
- Unit: acknowledgement gate blocks live actions until recorded.
- Unit: reduce-only flag set on revocation with open positions, cleared on flat.
- Contract: extended `AccountAccessGrantInput`/`AccountAccessGrant` schemas; session `allowed_environments`; `auth_ok` frame.
- Integration: revoke while positions are open, then assert close succeeds and open is refused; assert WS force-close on revoked scope.
- Migration test: default `false` for all existing rows; rollback tested.
- E2E (feeds E38-Q02): owner grants, manager acknowledges at sign-in, manager switches to live; then owner revokes and the manager sees reduce-only.
- Coverage: >=90% on the eligibility derivation module.

## Security notes
- This is a privilege-management surface: threats are elevation of privilege (self-grant, forged grant), bypass (acting on a grant before acknowledgement), and trapping a user in an unmanageable position (availability harm) - the reduce-only design addresses the last.
- Controls: owner-only `users:write` for eligibility, audited grant/revoke/acknowledge, enforcement at E38-T02's single choke point, additive migration defaulting to no access.
- The reason shown to a demo-only manager must not disclose other users' grants.
- `security` label mandatory (`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 8: anything touching RBAC). Abuse cases are exercised in E38-X02.

## Accessibility notes
- The eligibility control on SCR-122 has a clear current-state label and an accessible confirmation for a change that affects another person's capabilities.
- The acknowledgement prompt at sign-in is a focused, keyboard-operable dialog that cannot be dismissed by clicking away, with its consequences stated in text.

body:
## Context
US-PAPER-008 (Should) gives the owner a report of known demo-versus-live differences so expectations are calibrated, and it is the artefact that makes R4 'a gating exercise rather than a re-architecture' (roadmap section 7.1 goal 5). Its NFR forbids the easy implementation: 'the report is generated from a maintained data file plus runtime observations, never hand-written prose only'.

Three behaviours define it: list the known differences with their source and last-verified date; capture operations that fail only in demo as **candidate** parity items; and flag items unverified for 90 days as needing re-verification. The report lives in SCR-137 (Admin: security centre) and is linked from SCR-074.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Backend: load `packages/backend/cv/paper/parity_items.yaml` (seeded by E38-K01) at startup, validate it against a schema (id, area, description, source, severity, last_verified, capability_ref), and expose it via a new `GET /admin/parity` endpoint (add to `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, `x-rbac` permission `audit:read`, scope none).
- **Runtime observation capture**: every `CapabilityUnsupported` refusal (E38-T01) and every demo-only exchange error observed by the adapter is recorded as a *candidate* parity item with its operation, error signature, first-seen and last-seen timestamps and an occurrence count - deduplicated by signature, never auto-promoted into the confirmed list.
- **Staleness**: any confirmed item whose `last_verified` is older than 90 days is returned flagged `needs_reverification`; a scheduled job recomputes the flag daily and raises a notification when an item crosses the threshold.
- Re-verification action: an owner-only endpoint marking an item verified (updating `last_verified` and writing an audit row), intended to be driven by re-running the E38-K01 probe harness.
- Frontend on **SCR-137**: the parity table (difference, area, source, last verified, status), the needs-re-verification treatment using text plus icon, the candidate-items inbox with promote/dismiss actions, and empty/loading/error/RBAC-denied states. Components CMP-028, CMP-036, CMP-050, CMP-087, CMP-093, CMP-175, CMP-178.
- A link from SCR-074 to the report, so a user hitting a demo limitation can read why.
- Deep-link support: a `CapabilityUnsupported` refusal carries `parity_item_id`, and the UI links the refusal message to that row.

## Out of scope
- The probe harness that produces verification evidence (E38-K01 built it; this story only records the outcome).
- The paper-fidelity divergence panel (E38-T03 produces the data; its display reuses this screen's patterns but is a separate concern).
- Auto-promoting candidates to confirmed items - deliberately a human decision.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The report lists known differences with source and date
  Given the seeded parity data file
  When the report is requested
  Then each known difference is listed with its description, source and last-verified date, including no-WS-order-entry-in-demo, batch-order category limits and fee differences

Scenario: A demo-only failure becomes a candidate item
  Given an operation fails only in demo
  When the failure is observed at runtime
  Then it is recorded as a candidate parity item with its error signature and occurrence count, and is not silently merged into the confirmed list

Scenario: Stale items are flagged
  Given an item last verified 91 days ago
  When the report is generated
  Then that item is flagged as needing re-verification and a notification is raised once, not on every generation

Scenario: The report is generated, not authored
  Given the parity data file is modified
  When the report is requested
  Then the output reflects the file without any code change, and a test asserts no report content is hardcoded in the UI

Scenario: An invalid data file fails loudly at startup
  Given a parity item missing a required field
  When the application starts
  Then startup fails with a precise validation error rather than serving a silently incomplete report

Scenario: A refusal links to its parity item
  Given a capability refusal carrying a parity item id
  When the user follows the link
  Then the parity report opens focused on that row

Scenario: Re-verification is audited
  Given the owner marks an item verified
  When the change is saved
  Then last_verified updates and an audit row records who verified it and when
```

## Technical notes / design
- The data file is the source of truth and is version-controlled; the DB holds only runtime observations and verification timestamps, joined at read time. This keeps the curated knowledge reviewable in PRs while the observed knowledge accumulates at runtime.
- Candidate deduplication key: (operation, retCode, normalised retMsg) - normalise out ids and timestamps so one real difference is not recorded as thousands of candidates.
- The staleness notification uses the existing notification/alert delivery path rather than a bespoke mechanism.
- `capability_ref` cross-links each item to an `EnvironmentCapabilities` field, and a test asserts every hard capability restriction has a parity item and vice versa - this is what prevents the code and the report drifting apart.
- The UI renders whatever the API returns, including item types it does not know about, so adding a parity item never requires a frontend release.

## Test plan
- Unit: schema validation of the data file, incl. the startup-failure case.
- Unit: staleness computation at the 89/90/91-day boundaries.
- Unit: candidate deduplication and occurrence counting under repeated identical failures.
- Unit: capability-to-parity-item bidirectional coverage test.
- Contract: `GET /admin/parity` and the verification endpoint against OpenAPI; RBAC denial for non-`audit:read` callers.
- Integration: trigger a capability refusal through the adapter and assert a candidate item appears with the right signature.
- axe-core on the SCR-137 parity section incl. the flagged state.
- E2E (feeds E38-Q02): open the report, follow a deep link from a refusal, mark an item verified and observe the audit row.
- Coverage: >=85% backend, >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
- SCR-137 is the security centre: the report must contain no key material, no account identifiers beyond what the caller may already see, and no raw exchange responses that might embed credentials - candidate items store a normalised signature, not the raw payload.
- Access requires `audit:read`; verification requires owner-level permission and is audited.
- Threat: a stale or wrong parity report giving false confidence before R4 live enablement - mitigated by the staleness flag and the capability cross-link test.
- Data classification: operational/security metadata, internal.

## Accessibility notes
- Real table semantics with header associations; needs-re-verification and candidate states use text plus icon, never colour alone.
- The candidate inbox's promote/dismiss actions have accessible names naming the item.
- Deep-linked rows receive focus and are announced on arrival.
- Empty state explains what would populate the table rather than showing a bare 'no data'.

## Performance notes
- Tens of rows: no virtualisation needed. The report is assembled from an in-memory data file plus one indexed query; target <150 ms p95 (budget #13 read endpoints).
- Candidate recording must be fire-and-forget on the refusal path so it cannot add latency to an order rejection.

## Observability

- Notification when an item becomes stale, delivered once per transition.

title: Environment capability matrix and demo host routing in the exchange adapter
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` **SR-040a** is unambiguous: 'the environment capability matrix MUST be enforced in code, not documentation'. A single `ExchangeEnvironment` value selects an immutable capability record and every transport call asserts against it. Demo uses `api-demo.bybit.com` for orders only, has **no WS Trade** and **no public WS** (mainnet public streams supply market data), and limits batch orders to `linear`/`option`.

Threats W9 and W10 in the security program describe exactly what happens without this: a silent fallback or dual dispatch leaving orders unplaced or duplicated, and demo/live endpoints mixed within one session. This task makes both unreachable by construction and is the foundation every other E38 ticket stands on.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Add an immutable `EnvironmentCapabilities` record in `packages/backend/cv/exchange/capabilities.py`, keyed by `Environment` (`live`|`demo`|`testnet`, matching `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 1.2 and the Postgres `exchange_env` type), carrying: REST base URL, public WS URL (or `None`), private WS URL, `ws_trade_supported: bool`, `batch_order_categories: frozenset[str]`, `order_history_retention_days`, and the parity-item ids that justify each restriction.
- Wire the adapter (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 14 exchange adapter interface) so **one client instance exists per environment**, with no shared base-URL mutation - mixing endpoints in one session must be impossible by construction, not by convention.
- Every transport call asserts its capability before dispatch and raises `CapabilityUnsupported(operation, environment, parity_item_id)` when unsupported; there is no fallback path and no dual dispatch.
- Order entry is REST-only in **both** environments for v1 (WS Trade is an explicit non-goal); the code path is structured so that if WS Trade is ever enabled it is gated on `env == live` by the capability record.
- Public market-data subscriptions for a demo trading session resolve to the **mainnet** public streams, and this resolution is explicit and logged, not incidental.
- A CI assertion that no Bybit host string appears anywhere except `capabilities.py` (extending the SR-119 CSP assertion).
- Contract test `enum_parity_environment` continues to pass: `Environment` is identical across `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` and the PG type, and `paper` is a member of none of them.

## Out of scope
- The request-time isolation middleware for API routes (E38-T02).
- The local paper matcher (E38-S03).
- Any UI.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Demo order entry routes to the demo host
  Given a session whose environment is demo
  When an order is submitted through the adapter
  Then the request goes to api-demo.bybit.com and no mainnet order host is contacted

Scenario: WS trade on demo is unreachable
  Given the demo capability record
  When any code path attempts WS order entry
  Then a CapabilityUnsupported error is raised before any network call, and a unit test asserts no demo code path can reach a WS trade transport

Scenario: Batch order category restriction is enforced
  Given a demo session
  When a batch order is submitted for a category outside linear and option
  Then it is refused locally with the parity item id attached, without contacting the exchange

Scenario: Environments cannot be mixed in one session
  Given a live adapter client and a demo adapter client
  When their configurations are inspected at runtime
  Then they are separate instances with immutable base URLs, and a test asserting that mutating one leaves the other unchanged passes

Scenario: Market data for a demo session uses mainnet public streams
  Given a demo trading session
  When public market-data subscriptions are established
  Then they connect to the mainnet public stream host, and the resolution is recorded in a structured log line

Scenario: A new host cannot be introduced silently
  Given a developer adds a Bybit hostname outside capabilities.py
  When CI runs
  Then the host-location assertion fails the build
```

## Technical notes / design
- `EnvironmentCapabilities` is a frozen pydantic model constructed once at import; there is no setter and no environment variable that can override a URL at runtime (SR-004's spirit: transport identity is not configuration).
- `CapabilityUnsupported` maps to the RFC 9457 problem type used for refusals so the UI can render the plain-language message required by US-PAPER-001's 'Demo-only limitation' scenario; the problem body carries `parity_item_id` so the UI can deep-link into the parity report (E38-S08).
- Capability records reference `parity_items.yaml` ids produced by E38-K01, so the code and the user-facing report cannot drift apart - a capability with no matching parity item fails a unit test.
- Testnet is included in the enum for completeness but is used for smoke tests only per the locked decisions; its record mirrors demo unless K01 found otherwise.

## Test plan
- Unit: one test per capability field per environment; a parametrised test asserting every adapter operation checks a capability before dispatch (introspection over the adapter's method registry, so a newly added un-guarded method fails).
- Unit: `CapabilityUnsupported` carries a real parity item id that resolves in `parity_items.yaml`.
- Contract: `enum_parity_environment` (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 19.8) green.
- Integration: against recorded fixtures, a demo-configured adapter performs a full submit/amend/cancel cycle over REST and never opens a trade WS.
- CI gate: the Bybit-host location assertion.
- Coverage target: >=90% on `cv/exchange/capabilities.py` (this is safety-critical code, above the 85% floor).

## Security notes
- Directly implements **SR-040a**; supports **SR-119** (no exchange contact from the renderer; one chokepoint in the backend).
- Mitigates threats **W9** (tampering: assumed WS order entry on demo causing unplaced or duplicated orders) and **W10** (spoofing: mixed demo/live endpoints in one session).
- Data classification: no secrets in this module - it holds hosts and capability booleans only; credentials remain in the vault (E27).
- `security` label required; Security engineer review is mandatory before merge.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no UI. The user-facing message carried by `CapabilityUnsupported` is rendered accessibly by E38-S01.

## Performance notes
- Capability checks are dictionary lookups on frozen objects, resolved once per call; the added cost must be immeasurable against budget #4 (order submit to ack p95 <300 ms on demo). Assert with a microbenchmark that the guard adds <0.1 ms per call.

## Observability
- Structured log on adapter construction: environment, resolved REST host, resolved public WS host, `ws_trade_supported`.
- Counter `cv_capability_refusals_total{operation,environment}` - a non-zero value on live is an alertable anomaly.
- Every `CapabilityUnsupported` is logged at warning with the operation and parity item id, and feeds the runtime-detected candidate parity items in E38-S08.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria demonstrated by automated tests referencing each scenario by name.
- [ ] Coverage: >=85% lines on touched backend/engine packages, >=80% on touched frontend packages; CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] Docs updated: `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`, `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md`, `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` reflect shipped behaviour where they diverged.

title: Server-side environment isolation middleware with 403 and high-severity audit
body:
## Context
US-PAPER-003 is a Must: 'every trading-capable view gated by environment, so that the two can never mix', with the explicit NFR 'enforced in one middleware layer with tests covering every trading route'. Its third scenario is the hard one: **a crafted request targeting a live account from a demo session must be rejected with 403 and audited as a high-severity event**.

US-PAPER-002's NFR adds that 'environment is part of every trading request; a mismatch between client intent and server session is rejected'. The client-side guard CMP-139 is defence in depth only - this task is the real boundary. It is also the environment leg of the RBAC 4-tuple `(permission, account scope, symbol allowance, environment enabled)` from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` section 7.

## Scope / Deliverables
- One FastAPI dependency/middleware in `packages/backend/cv/api/deps/environment.py` applied to **every** mutating trading route: `POST /orders`, `PATCH /orders/{orderId}`, `DELETE /orders/{orderId}`, `POST /orders/cancel-all`, `POST /trade-groups`, `POST /trade-groups/{id}/amend`, `POST /trade-groups/{id}/cancel`, `POST /trade-groups/preview`, `POST /positions/{id}/tpsl`, `POST /positions/{id}/close`, `POST /positions/{id}/reverse`, `POST /positions/{id}/leverage`, `POST /positions/close-all`, `POST /rules/{ruleId}/mode` (arming), `POST /alerts/{alertId}/enabled` where the alert has a trading action, and `POST /trading/kill-switch`.
- The check: resolve the target account(s) from the request, read their `env` from `exchange_accounts` (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` section 3.2), compare against the session's active environment and the user's `allowed_environments`; any mismatch is a `403` RFC 9457 problem with a stable error code and **no state change**.
- **Mixed-group prevention**: reject creation of, and submission to, any trade group whose member accounts do not all share one `env` - enforced both at `POST /trade-groups` and at submit, complementing the existing DB constraint `tg_paper_env` and the `trg_ea_env_parent` trigger.
- Audit every rejection as a high-severity event with the attempted environment, the session environment, the target account and the route; emit on the `system` WS topic so the admin security centre sees it live.
- A **route-coverage test** that enumerates the OpenAPI document, selects every route tagged `trading` (or otherwise account-mutating), and asserts each one carries the environment dependency - a newly added trading route without the guard fails CI.

## Out of scope
- The switch endpoint itself (E38-S02).
- Per-user live eligibility grants (E38-S07) - this middleware consumes `allowed_environments`, it does not manage it.
- Frontend guarding (CMP-139, E38-S04).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Crafted cross-environment request is refused and audited
  Given a session whose active environment is demo
  When a request is crafted targeting a live exchange account
  Then the response is 403, no order is created, and an audit row of high severity is written naming both environments and the target account

Scenario: Every trading route is covered
  Given the generated OpenAPI document
  When the route-coverage test runs
  Then every account-mutating route has the environment dependency attached, and adding a new trading route without it fails CI

Scenario: Mixed-environment trade group is impossible
  Given a set of accounts containing one demo and one live account
  When a trade group is created from them
  Then creation is refused with 422, and a separate test asserts submission to an already-existing mixed group is also refused

Scenario: Environment mismatch between client intent and session
  Given a request that explicitly declares environment live
  And a session whose active environment is demo
  When the request is processed
  Then it is rejected before reaching the OMS, with the mismatch named in the problem detail

Scenario: A user without the environment grant cannot use it
  Given a manager whose allowed_environments contains only demo
  When any live-targeting request is made, even with a valid live account id
  Then it is refused with 403 and audited, regardless of the session's claimed environment

Scenario: Rejections do not leak other users' grants
  Given a refusal caused by a missing live grant
  When the problem detail is inspected
  Then it states only that the caller lacks live access, never who does have it
```

## Technical notes / design
- The dependency runs **after** authentication and permission resolution but **before** any handler body, so no partial work is possible; it is implemented as a FastAPI dependency returning a resolved `EnvironmentContext` that handlers must accept, making omission a type error rather than a silent gap.
- Account resolution differs per route (body field, path param, trade-group membership); implement per-route extractors registered in one table, so the extractor list is reviewable in one place.
- Error codes reuse the existing registry (`docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` error registry) - add `environment_mismatch` and `environment_not_permitted` there rather than inventing ad hoc strings; the registry is single-source and has its own contract test.
- Audit rows go through the existing append-only hash-chained audit writer (E42/`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md`), with event name `trading.environment_mismatch_rejected` at high severity.
- The WS broadcast piggybacks on the `system` topic already used for environment switch notifications.

## Test plan
- Unit: matrix over (session env, target account env, allowed_environments) covering all combinations incl. the testnet value; assert 403 + no side effect + audit row for every disallowed cell.
- Unit: mixed-group rejection at create and at submit.
- Contract: OpenAPI route-coverage test described above; error-registry test for the two new codes.
- Integration: against a seeded DB with one demo and one live account, drive each listed route with a crafted cross-environment payload and assert 403 with zero rows written to `orders`/`positions`.
- E2E (feeds E38-Q02): the crafted-request scenario end to end, asserting the admin security centre shows the event.
- Chaos-adjacent: assert the guard still refuses when the audit writer is unavailable - it must fail closed (refuse) rather than fail open.
- Coverage target: >=90% on the middleware module.

## Security notes
- Implements the environment leg of the RBAC 4-tuple (`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` section 7, `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 15.2) and US-PAPER-003's server-enforcement scenario.
- Threats: elevation of privilege (demo user reaching live), tampering (crafted account id), repudiation (an attempt with no audit trail). Controls: single choke point, fail-closed audit, high-severity event, route-coverage CI gate.
- Data classification: request metadata and account ids; no secrets. Problem details must not disclose other users' grants (information disclosure).
- `security` label mandatory; per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 8 this ticket cannot reach Done without a Security engineer review comment and a manual privilege-escalation abuse check.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no UI. The 403 problem details are rendered by the frontend with the accessible disabled-with-reason pattern (E38-S04).

## Performance notes
- The guard adds one already-cached account lookup per request; assert p95 added latency <5 ms so budget #13 (write endpoints <300 ms p95 backend-internal) is unaffected. Account `env` is read from the request-scoped account cache, never a fresh query per leg of a fan-out.

## Observability

title: Nightly paper-versus-demo fill divergence job and fidelity panel data
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 12.5 states the requirement plainly: 'The paper matcher's honesty is verified, not assumed.' A nightly job replays a recorded day through the matcher while comparing against the demo account's real fills for the same period where they overlap, reporting mean and p95 slippage difference, fill-rate difference for resting limits and fee difference. A p95 slippage divergence above one tick or a fill-rate divergence above 10 pp opens a defect ticket against the fill model, and results are shown on the admin 'Paper fidelity' panel.

Without this job, US-PAPER-004's simulator is an unfalsifiable claim, and R12 (backtest bias) has no control at all.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Scheduled job in `packages/backend/cv/paper/divergence.py`: for each symbol with both recorded market data and real demo fills in the window, replay the recorded day through the `PaperMatcher` using the same order stream the demo account actually submitted, and compare outcomes.
- Metrics computed per symbol and overall: mean and p95 slippage difference (in ticks), fill-rate difference for resting limit orders (percentage points), fee difference, and count of orders compared.
- Threshold evaluation: p95 slippage divergence >1 tick or fill-rate divergence >10 pp raises a defect - emit an alert and create a tracked issue record (not silently logged).
- Persist results as a dated document queryable by the admin fidelity panel; expose via `GET /admin/paper-fidelity` (add to `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, `x-rbac` permission `audit:read`).
- Handle the honest edge cases: no overlap (report 'insufficient data', never a fabricated zero divergence), too few comparable orders for a meaningful p95 (report the sample size and suppress the threshold check), and symbols where recording gaps make the replay unfaithful (detect via `GET /market/data-coverage` and exclude with a stated reason).
- Update `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 12.5 and `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` section 3.7 if the implemented metric definitions differ from the written ones, and record any fill-model decision made during implementation as an ADR amendment.

## Out of scope
- The fidelity panel UI beyond the API (its design is E38-D03; the rendering is folded into E38-S08's SCR-137 patterns or filed as a follow-up if capacity is short).
- Automatically tuning the fill model from divergence results - tuning is a human decision informed by the report.
- Comparing against *live* fills (there are none in R3).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Divergence is computed over overlapping activity
  Given a recorded day with both market data and real demo fills
  When the nightly job runs
  Then mean and p95 slippage difference, resting-limit fill-rate difference and fee difference are computed and persisted with the compared-order count

Scenario: Breaching a threshold raises a defect
  Given a p95 slippage divergence above one tick
  When the job evaluates thresholds
  Then an alert is raised and a tracked defect record is created against the fill model, not merely logged

Scenario: Insufficient data is reported, not fabricated
  Given a day with no overlapping demo fills
  When the job runs
  Then the result states insufficient data with the reason, and no divergence figure is reported

Scenario: Small samples suppress the threshold check
  Given fewer comparable orders than the configured minimum
  When the job evaluates thresholds
  Then the sample size is reported and the threshold check is skipped with that stated, rather than firing on noise

Scenario: Recording gaps exclude a symbol honestly
  Given a symbol whose recorded coverage has gaps in the window
  When the job selects symbols
  Then that symbol is excluded with the gap named, because an unfaithful replay would produce a meaningless comparison

Scenario: Results are queryable by date
  Given several nights of results
  When the fidelity endpoint is queried for a date range
  Then each night's metrics are returned with their thresholds and outcomes
```

## Technical notes / design
- The job reuses the replay engine (E26) and the same event bus as production, so the comparison exercises the real matcher rather than a test double - this is the whole point of the architecture's shared-bus design (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 13).
- Slippage difference is computed per order as (simulated average fill price - real average fill price) expressed in ticks, signed so a systematically optimistic simulator is visible as a consistent direction rather than cancelling out in the mean; report both mean (bias) and p95 (tail).
- Fill-rate difference applies only to resting limit orders, where queue modelling is the uncertain part; market orders are compared on slippage only.
- The job is idempotent per (date, symbol) so a re-run overwrites rather than duplicating.
- Runs off-peak and is cancellable; it must never contend with live ingestion for CPU.

## Test plan
- Unit: metric computations against hand-computed fixtures, incl. the sign convention for bias.
- Unit: threshold evaluation at the boundary (exactly 1 tick, exactly 10 pp) and under the minimum sample size.
- Unit: insufficient-data and coverage-gap paths produce explicit reasons.
- Unit: idempotent re-run.
- Integration: a seeded recorded day plus fixture demo fills produces a full report document; a deliberately mis-tuned fill model produces a threshold breach and a defect record.
- Contract: the fidelity endpoint against OpenAPI.
- Coverage: >=85%.

## Security notes
- The job reads recorded market data and the account's own fills; no credential use beyond the existing fee-rate lookups.
- Threat: a silently failing job giving false assurance that the simulator is honest. Control: the job's own liveness is monitored and a missed night alerts - absence of a report is treated as a failure, not as a pass.
- Data classification: trading data, internal.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - backend job. Its output is rendered on SCR-137 following that screen's accessibility rules.

## Performance notes
- Must complete within the off-peak window for a full day of the recorded symbol set; target under 30 minutes for 10 symbols, leaning on the matcher's 20x-faster-than-real-time requirement from E38-S03.
- Must not exceed the per-symbol backend memory budget #8 while replaying.

## Observability
- Metrics `cv_paper_divergence_slippage_ticks{symbol,stat}`, `cv_paper_divergence_fill_rate_pp{symbol}`, `cv_paper_divergence_job_duration_seconds`, `cv_paper_divergence_job_last_success_timestamp`.
- Alert on threshold breach and on a missed run (stale last-success timestamp).
- Structured log of the `FillModelConfig` used, so a breach is attributable to a configuration as well as to code.

## Scope / Deliverables

  1. Craft a live-targeting request from a demo session via every trading route (driven from the route list in E38-T02), including direct API calls bypassing the UI entirely.
  2. Attempt to switch to live without step-up, with an expired elevation, with the `live_trading` flag off, and by replaying a previously successful switch request.
  3. Attempt to act on a live grant before acknowledgement.
  4. Attempt self-granting of live eligibility as a manager, and via a crafted `PUT /users/{userId}/account-access` payload targeting one's own user id.
  5. Attempt to create and to submit a mixed-environment trade group.
  6. Attempt to make the paper matcher perform a network call (dependency injection, config override, monkeypatch-style manipulation of the adapter routing).
  7. Attempt to reset a live account's balance via the paper-reset endpoint.
  8. Attempt to read another user's grants through the not-permitted message, the parity report or an error body.
  9. Attempt to flood candidate parity items to exhaust storage.
- Verify for each: refusal, no state change, an audit row of the right severity, and no information leaked in the response.
- Commit durable detections: Semgrep rules forbidding (a) a Bybit hostname outside `capabilities.py`, (b) a trading route handler without the environment dependency, (c) an HTTP/WS client import inside `cv/paper/`; plus a ZAP/DAST profile exercising the cross-environment routes.
- Run SCA and secrets scanning over the new code paths and triage findings.

## Out of scope
- The threat model itself (E38-X01) and the final review (E38-X03).
- Pen-testing (E43, an R4 activity) - this is internal abuse-case testing, deliberately narrower.
- Load-based denial of service beyond the candidate-item flood case (E38-Q03 covers capacity).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin

  Given the abuse-case list from the threat model
  When testing completes
  Then each case has a recorded outcome with evidence, and any success is filed as a priority p0 security defect

Scenario: Cross-environment attempts are refused on every route
  Given the full trading route list
  When a live-targeting request is crafted from a demo session on each
  Then every route refuses with 403, changes no state, and writes a high-severity audit row

Scenario: The simulator cannot be made to reach the network
  Given attempts to route the paper matcher through a real transport
  When each is tried
  Then none succeeds, and the structural Semgrep rule prevents the import that would enable it

Scenario: Self-granting is impossible
  Given a manager account
  When eligibility self-grant is attempted directly against the API
  Then it is refused and audited, and the attempt does not partially apply

Scenario: Durable rules are committed and run in CI
  When this ticket completes
  Then the three Semgrep rules and the ZAP profile are committed and executing in CI, failing the build on violation

Scenario: A replayed switch request does not re-switch
  Given a captured successful switch request
  When it is replayed after the elevation expires
  Then it is refused rather than honoured
```

- Testing is black-box against staging plus white-box review of the isolation middleware, the adapter routing and the eligibility derivation - the combination matters because a route can pass black-box testing while having the guard attached in a way a refactor would silently drop.
- The route-list-driven approach means this test automatically covers routes added after E38-T02 was written, as long as the OpenAPI document is the source.
- Semgrep rules are written to fail on the *pattern*, not on a filename allowlist, so moving a file does not defeat them.
- Evidence for each case: request, response, database state before and after, and the audit row (or its absence, which is itself a finding).

## Test plan
- The abuse cases are the test artefact. Each durable rule must be demonstrated to fire against a deliberately introduced violation before it is accepted.
